However, you can sell your discounted Singtel shares, in which the sale proceeds will be credited into your CPF Ordinary Account.To sell, please log in tomy cpf Online Serviceswith your Singpass > Select my cpf > My dashboards > Investment, look under “Discounted Singtel Shares” section and click on “Sell your shares”.

questions.question: Will I run the risk of unknowingly breaching CPF laws while trading or investing under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: As long as your intention is to invest for the medium to long term, and you did not siphon out any CPF savings by receiving cash for your investment transactions whether through manipulated transaction prices or cash rebates, it is unlikely that you will breach the CPF laws for manipulative transactions.

questions.question: What enhancements relating to CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) were announced during the FY2018 Committee of Supply Debate?
questions.answer: Second Minister for Manpower Josephine Teo announced the following enhancements to the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS):Introduction of Self-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)(PDF, 0.6MB)Removal of sales charge for products offered under CPFIS(PDF, 0.6MB)Reduction of maximum wrap fee chargeable on CPFIS investments(PDF, 0.5MB)Please refer to ourwebpagefor more details of the enhancements.

questions.question: Who can I approach if I want to know more on the trailer fees of the CPF Investment Scheme products?
questions.answer: You can approach your product/service provider or financial advisors for more information on trailer fees.

questions.question: What if I prefer making MediSave contributions through the current payment modes (e.g. GIRO)?
questions.answer: The small and regular MediSave contributions made through Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) help self-employed persons (SEPs) to reduce the MediSave contributions payable in the following year (after SEPs declare their Net Trade Income and have their MediSave payable computed).If you’ve made your MediSave contributions in full or are on GIRO instalment plan, you’ll be allowed to set your CAYE contribution rate to 0% and receive your service fee in full.

questions.question: I am a freelancer/conducting a home business (e.g. baking, sewing). Can I qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme?
questions.answer: To qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme, please declare your net trade income as a self-employed person and contribute to your MediSave Account. You will also need to meet theWIS eligibility criteriain order to qualify for WIS.To conduct a home business, you need to follow the guidelines under HDB's Home-Based Small-Scale Business Scheme. Please refer to theHousing Development Board's websitefor more information.

questions.question: How do I stop receiving the CPF Contribution Alert via CPF Mobile app?
questions.answer: You candisable personalised notificationsat CPF Mobile app Settings page.

questions.question: What will happen to my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme investments if I did not open a CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account in time for the transfer?
questions.answer: As indicated in the National University of Singapore (NUS) letter to you, if you did not open a CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account by 27 December 2007, NUS is unable to transfer your Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (ASPFAIS-OA) investment holdings and Part V insurance policies. As the Academic Staff Provident Fund (ASPF) scheme has closed down, your ASPFAIS Investment Account has been frozen and you will no longer be able to use your ASPF monies to transact under the ASPFAIS and service the premiums of your insurance policies bought under the ASPF Part V Scheme.You can still open a CPFIS Investment Account at any agent bank i.e. DBS, OCBC and UOB, and instruct NUS to transfer your ASPFAIS investments and Part V insurance policies to your newly-opened CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) Investment Accountafter 1 January 2008. However, this transfer will be effected only on a monthly basis and any payments to be made in the meantime, including insurance premiums, would have to be paid in cash.For your investments bought under Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme - Special Account (ASPFAIS-SA), NUS would have transferred them over to CPF Investment - Special Account (CPFIS-SA) as long as you have a CPF Account. No CPFIS Investment Account is needed for the transfer of investment holdings under the SA.

questions.question: What if my banking app is unable to scan the PayNow QR for my top-up application?
questions.answer: If you are having trouble scanning the PayNow QR code for your top-up application, you should reach out to your bank for assistance.

questions.question: Are CPF contributions payable on the National Service (NS) make-up pay when I am away from work for NS training?
questions.answer: Your employer should continue to pay CPF contributions on the total wages payable to you, as if you are not away for the NS training. The basic salary and fixed allowance components of your wages, as well as the variable allowances (e.g. overtime pay and allowances) typically paid to you on a monthly basis, as shown in payslips, would attract CPF contributions.ExampleTim earns a basic salary of $2,000 and an average overtime pay of $800 every month. He went on NS training for one week in July.Tim’s employer will have to pay CPF contributions on his typical total monthly wage of $2,800. The employee’s share of CPF contributions will also be based on the total wages of $2,800, and Tim’s employer is entitled to recover this from Tim’s wages.

questions.question: Will I still receive the full matching grant of $2,000 if my retirement savings exceed the current Basic Retirement Sum after topping up?
questions.answer: Yes, you will receive the full matching grant of $2,000 as long as you are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme for the year, and the total amount of cash top-ups you received was at least $2,000.

questions.question: Why am I not able to top up my Special/Retirement Account beyond the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS) (below 55) or Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) (55 or above)?
questions.answer: The CPF system is designed to cater to the basic retirement needs of the broad majority of Singaporeans.If you are below 55, you can top up your Special Account up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS) to build up your retirement savings. If you wish to save beyond the FRS, you can choose to tap on theSupplementary Retirement Scheme, where contributions are also eligible for tax relief.If you are 55 or above, retirement becomes a higher priority. As such, members have the option to voluntarily top up beyond the FRS up to thecurrent year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)for higher payouts. This could help the middle-income group better meet their retirement needs.Find out more aboutwhat the retirement sums are.

questions.question: When will I need to be registered for PayNow to continue receiving my net service fee payments without delay?
questions.answer: PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) will be the default payment mode from early June 2024. Please ensure that you are registered for PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) so that you receive your service fee payments promptly.

questions.question: How do I transfer my shares, bought under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), to my Central Depository (CDP) account?
questions.answer: You can apply to withdraw your CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments and transfer your shares to your own CDP account, after you have reached 55 years old and have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in the Retirement Account (RA). The FRS can be set aside fully with cash, or with cash (i.e. at least the Basic Retirement Sum) and property. Your CPF Investment Account will be closed once you apply to withdraw your investments.Please refer to thisFAQfor more information on how the retirement sum is set aside at age 55.You will be able to view the link to submit your application through theInvestment dashboardif you meet the eligibility conditions.

questions.question: If I am concurrently a full-time employee doing platform work, will my employers be notified of my platform work because of the CPF contributions?
questions.answer: No. Your employers will not be notified of your CPF contributions from platform work.

questions.question: How does the company I contracted with know my Net Trade Income information and/or Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate?
questions.answer: The company which you have contracted with will not have access to your Net Trade Income information. CPF Board will only inform the company of the amount that they would have to deduct from your service fee and transmit to your MediSave Account.

questions.question: How will I know when my digital notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons is ready for viewing?
questions.answer: You will receive an email notification to view your digital notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons via the self-employment dashboard when it is ready. If you do not have a registered email with CPF Board, you will receive an SMS notification instead. If you do not have a registered email address or mobile number, your notice will be sent to you in hardcopy at your residential address.To ensure you receive prompt alerts when your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons is ready, please update your contact details via theaccount services pageafter logging in with your Singpass.

questions.question: Will I be charged if my friend conducts manipulative share trading using my CPF and trading accounts (given by me previously) without my knowing?
questions.answer: This will depend on the outcome of investigations.  However, you should always protect your password and not allow other people to transact in your name without your knowledge or your approval.

questions.question: As a self-employed person, how will the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme affect me?
questions.answer: Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) helps you save for your healthcare needs through smaller and more regular MediSave contributions each time you receive a payment. There is no change to your MediSave contributions payable as it would still be based on your actual Net Trade Income.

questions.question: How does the closure of my Special Account affect the amount of tax relief that I can earn when I top up my Retirement Account in cash?
questions.answer: Cash top-ups to your Retirement Account (RA) up to the current year’sFull Retirement Sum (FRS)can qualify for tax relief of up to $8,000 per year. This will continue even after your Special Account (SA) is closed.For information, when members turn 55, their savings in their SA and Ordinary Account (OA) are transferred to their RA, up to their applicable FRS. The applicable FRS is the FRS in year they turn 55 and remains fixed for them thereafter, even when the FRS increases each year. Hence, members who have met their applicable FRS may still qualify for tax relief on their top-ups as the current year’s FRS may be higher than their applicable FRS.Illustration:Mr Lim turns 55 in 2024. His applicable FRS is $205,800. Assume he has $200,000 transferred from his SA and OA to his RA when he turns 55. He decides to make a cash top-up of $5,800 to his RA to meet his FRS in 2024. He can qualify for tax relief for his $5,800 top-up.In 2025, Mr Lim’s SA will be closed and his SA savings will be transferred to his OA since he has met his applicable FRS. However, as the FRS for 2025 is $213,000, he can get a tax relief of up to $7,200 (i.e. $213,000 - $205,800) if he makes additional cash top-ups to his RA.

questions.question: What incentives are there for me to top up to my loved ones under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme when the tax relief is removed from 2025?
questions.answer: Topping up to your loved ones’ CPF accounts helps them to build up more retirement savings and increases their monthly payouts in retirement. From 1 January 2025, recipients of cash top-ups who are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) can also receive a matching grant of up to $2,000 per year (an increase from $600 per year) from the Government, which will further boost their retirement savings.You may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract MRSS matching grants ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).Learn more onhow this works.

questions.question: What if platform operators discriminate against workers who are mandated or opt in to increased CPF contributions, such as through job allocation or incentives?
questions.answer: Due to the cohort-based approach where it is mandatory for all platform workers born in 1995 or later to make CPF contributions aligned with that of employees, an increasing proportion of platform workers will be making the increased contributions. It would be advantageous for platform operators in the long term to treat all workers fairly, regardless of whether they opt in, are in the mandatory cohort, or do not opt in.Platform workers also have the option of switching between platform operators. It is therefore in the interest of platform operators to treat all workers fairly from the perspective of worker retention.Tripartite partners will be including additional guidelines in the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices to provide greater clarity that intermediaries such as platform operators should not discriminate based on characteristics that are not related to the job, including when allocating work to platform workers.Finally, Platform Work Associations will have the legal mandate to represent the interests of platform workers. If there are instances of possible discriminatory practices by any platform operator, Platform Work Associations can take this up with the relevant platform operators and, where necessary, inform MOM.

questions.question: How does each taxi operator know the Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution amount?
questions.answer: CPF Board will inform participating taxi operators of taxi principal hirers who qualify1for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions monthly. The amount of contribution made by hirers will not be revealed.Please note that eligibility for co-contribution is subject to terms and conditions determined by taxi operators.1Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions as self-employed persons viaManage your MediSave payableorGIRO.

questions.question: I have updated my preference via the notification preference form. Does this preference apply to other notifications sent by CPF Board?
questions.answer: The notification preference only applies to the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons. Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions thereafter.

questions.question: How would I know if I would make a gain or loss if I were to sell my discounted Singtel shares now?
questions.answer: For sale of discounted Singtel shares, you can use theweighted average cost (WAC) methodto determine whether you would make a gain or loss.

questions.question: Can I transfer my top-ups made to my Special Account/ Retirement Account to other CPF accounts if I need to use them for other purposes such as housing or healthcare?
questions.answer: No, such cash top-ups and CPF transfers are meant to boost your retirement savings to enable you to receive higher payouts. Hence, they cannot be used for other purposes or transferred to other CPF accounts such as your Ordinary Account or MediSave Account.Consider whether you would require the monies for other purposes (e.g. housing or healthcare expenses) before topping up to your Special Account/ Retirement Account.

questions.question: What should I do if my platform operator did not pay me the correct amount of earnings and CPF contributions?
questions.answer: ThePlatform Workers Actrequires your platform operator to provide you with an itemised earnings slip, which will include any deductions from your earnings. You should verify the CPF paid as declared by your platform operator against the deductions shown in your earnings slip.If there are any discrepancies or if you have any clarifications, please approach your platform operator immediately so that any errors can be rectified early while documentary evidence is fresh. Your platform operator is expected to self-rectify any errors immediately.If you were not paid the right amount of earnings, you should approach your union if your platform operator is unionised or if you are a union member for advice. If you are not a union member, you could approach the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) for advice.Once TADM has concluded assessing your claims and determined the earnings due to you, you can lodge a report with CPF Board. The Board will compute the CPF contributions payable.

questions.question: Why do Self-Employed Persons receive only two-thirds of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) received by employees?
questions.answer: The CPF contribution made by Self-Employed Persons (SEPs) is comparatively less than employees who earn the same amount. SEPs are only required to contribute to their MediSave Account whereas employees need to contribute to all their CPF Accounts (Ordinary, Special and MediSave Accounts).

questions.question: I have set up a GIRO arrangement to make top-ups to my spouse or sibling before 16 February 2024. With the increase in income threshold from $4,000 to $8,000, how can I amend my instructions for the GIRO arrangement to claim tax relief?
questions.answer: The increase in income threshold for tax relief for cash top-ups to spouse or sibling will apply to cash top-ups made on 1 January 2024 or after. If you have a GIRO arrangement to make regular cash top-ups to your spouse or sibling and instructed to not claim tax relief previously, you cansubmit an applicationto amend your instructions to claim tax relief for top-ups from 2024 onwards.

questions.question: Do I still need to declare my income to IRAS and contribute MediSave in the following year for my self-employed work?
questions.answer: From 2025, if you are only receiving platform earnings in the year, platform operators would have deducted and paid the CPF contributions on your platform earnings for you every month. Therefore, you do not need to make your own MediSave contributions on such platform earnings in the following year.If you derive self-employed income from non-platform work (e.g. giving tuition, or taxi street-hail jobs), you will still need to pay MediSave contributions on these sources of income in the following year on your own, as per status quo, after you have declared your net trade income to IRAS. CPF Board will notify you of the MediSave contributions you need to make.For tax purposes, you will still need to declare your net trade income derived from platform work and any non-platform work in the year as a self-employed person (SEP) toIRAS.

questions.question: I have adjusted my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate. When will the updated rate take effect?
questions.answer: Generally, your updated Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate will apply to service fees paid from the next day.

questions.question: Why is there a lifetime cap of $20,000 to the matching grant when the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is enhanced from 2025?
questions.answer: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is targeted at seniors with lesser means and lower retirement savings to help them save more for retirement. The enhancements to provide $2,000 matching grant annually, capped at $20,000 over a lifetime, are a significant increase from the current scheme, and can increase eligible seniors’ CPF savings by at least $48,000 in 10 years, which translates to about a $260 increase in monthly CPF payouts*.While it may not help all eligible seniors meet the Basic Retirement Sum, it is part of a broader set of schemes providing retirement adequacy support. Other schemes, such as the Majulah Package and the Silver Support Scheme, will also help boost the retirement adequacy of seniors.*Estimation for a male member who starts payout at age 65 on the CPF LIFE Standard Plan.

questions.question: What is the difference between the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) and CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA)?
questions.answer: Under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA), investments may only be made using Ordinary Account savings while under CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA), investments may only be made using Special Account savings. The instruments available for investments under CPFIS-OA and CPFIS-SA are different.To find out how much CPF savings you can invest and whatinstruments youcan invest in, you can refer to thelist of instruments available for investment under the CPFIS(PDF, 0.1MB).

questions.question: How is my voluntary housing refund used to set aside my Retirement Sum if I am 55 years old and above?
questions.answer: The refunded amount will be used to meet your cohort's Full Retirement Sum (FRS) if you’re 55 years old and have not met the FRS. Please refer to the example below on how the voluntary housing refund is used to meet your FRS.ExampleAssumptions:1. You turned 55 years old in 20232. Your cohort’s Full Retirement Sum is $198,8003. You have received less than $30,000 in housing grantsCurrent RA balance$98,800Current OA balance$100,000Principal amount withdrawn for the property and the accrued interest (P+I)$500,000If you make a voluntary housing refund of $200,000New RA balanceThe vHR of $100,000 is used to top up to RA to meet the cohort’s FRS$198,800New OA balanceThe remaining vHR of $100,000 remains in OA after topping up RA to meet FRSThe balance in OA can continued to be used for housing payments$200,000Revised P+IThe vHR of $200,000 is used to reduce the P+I$300,000

questions.question: Why is my spouse's Assessable Income for the preceding Year of Assessment used to determine my Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) eligibility for the current work year?
questions.answer: This is to allow potential Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) recipients to receive WIS earlier despite the time needed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for the processing and transmission of Assessable Income (AI) to the CPF Board.The AI for the previous Year of Assessment (YOA) is used to assess one's WIS eligibility for the current year. E.g. we will use your spouse's AI for YOA 2022 to assess your eligibility for 2023 WIS.

questions.question: Why will Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) cease in 2029?
questions.answer: Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is meant to offset the increase in the platform workers’ share of CPF contributions in the transition phase as platform workers’ CPF contributions are gradually aligned with that of employees over five years. In 2029, when platform worker’s CPF contributions are completely aligned with that of employees, PCTS will cease.Eligible lower-income platform workers can tap on the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) instead, where platform workers will receive higher WIS payments at the same level as employees from 2029, once their CPF contribution rates fully align with that of employees. They will also receive a higher proportion of WIS payments in cash – 40% compared to 10% today.

questions.question: How soon can I sell my investments which are traded on the Singapore Exchange after I buy them under the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account?
questions.answer: You can sell your investments (e.g. shares or property funds) which are listed on the Singapore Exchange one trading day after the purchase date provided:Your stock broker has keyed the purchase trade on the day the purchase contract is made; andYou have sufficient investible funds in your CPF Investment and/or Ordinary Account to settle the purchase.Your available stock limit or gold limit will be updated on the 2nd trading day (i.e. T+2) based on the cost of the shares, property funds, corporate bonds or gold exchange traded funds (ETFs) sold when the sale transaction is settled. Please refer to thisexample(PDF, 0.1MB) to see how the stock limit and gold limit are computed.Can I reinvest the full sale proceeds immediately?If you intend to buy another share, property fund, corporate bond or gold ETF during this T+2 period, please check with your agent bank on your available stock limit or gold limit first. You will need to have sufficient investible funds in your CPF Investment and/or Ordinary Account to settle the new purchase before the settlement deadline.Why can’t I reinvest the full sale proceeds immediately?You have to ensure that you have the sufficient limits, and monies to reinvest when your sale proceeds have been refunded. Unlike cash trades, stock investment using CPF is subject to the CPF stock limit which may change with CPF contributions, withdrawals, crediting of CPFIS sale proceeds, new CPFIS investments etc. Hence, to err on the safe side, it may be better for you to reinvest after your fund position is firmed up on T+2, in line with SGX settlement framework.

questions.question: If I previously withdrew from my Retirement Account by pledging my property, what happens to my pledged property after I make a voluntary housing refund?
questions.answer: You will need to refund the amount you previously pledged if the voluntary housing refund is not enough to meet the Full Retirement Sum in your Retirement Account. Check the amount you need to refund under “What happens if” of yourHome ownership dashboard.

questions.question: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if my monthly income is above $4,000.
questions.answer: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is designed to help senior Singapore Citizens with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts. The average monthly income of $4,000 will cover most senior workers. If your average monthly income is above $4,000, you will not be eligible for the scheme as it is intended to provide additional support to those who need it the most.

questions.question: Do top-up monies form part of the required $40,000 that needs to be set aside before I can invest my Special Account monies?
questions.answer: Top-up monies form part of the $40,000 that needs to be set aside in the Special Account (SA) before you can use the excess for your investment. However, top-up monies cannot be used for investment. For example, if you have $100,000 in your SA, of which $90,000 are top up monies you received in your SA, only monies in excess of the $90,000 (i.e. $10,000) can be invested. Please refer to thisFAQfor further information on usage of top-up monies.

questions.question: How do I apply to adjust my CPF Contributions from the firm's account to a self-employed person's account?
questions.answer: You may submit an online application viamy cpfdigital servicesusing Singpass to adjust your CPF Contributions from the firm’s account to your self-employed account.The adjustment request must be made within one year from the date of payment.

questions.question: How can I make cash top-ups to my child's CPF retirement savings?
questions.answer: To make cash top-ups to your child's CPF retirement savings (regardless his or her age), simply:1. Indicate your identification number as the giver of the cash top-up in the application2. Indicate your child's identification number as the recipient3. Select the relationship as "Others"Do note that givers of cash top-ups need to be at least 16 years old andcash top-ups to children will not qualify for tax relief.Find out more about the types ofcash top-ups which can enjoy tax relief.

questions.question: How can I declare my net trade income from Work Year 2023 (Year of Assessment 2024) onwards?
questions.answer: For Work Year 2023 (WY2023) onwardsAll Net Trade Income (NTI) declarations for Work Year 2023 (Year of Assessment 2024) can be made with the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) by filing a tax return. There is no need to file separate declarations with CPF Board.If you receive a notification (via letter/form/SMS) to file tax from IRAS, or you meet the requirement to file tax (i.e. NTI above $6,000 and/or Total Income above $22,000), please complete and submit the tax return to IRAS directly. The income tax filing period is from 1 March to 18 April annually.If you do not receive a notification from IRAS or do not meet the requirement to file tax, you can declare your self-employed net trade income (NTI) to IRAS viamyTax Portalwhich will be available from 1 March to 31 October annually for taxpayers to e-File tax returns.Once IRAS has assessed your income for the year, your assessed NTI will be transmitted to the Board. You can check your updated NTI records by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard with your Singpass.If you have declared your NTI with IRAS, you need not declare your income again to CPF Board.

questions.question: Can my insurance policy continue to run on Automatic Premium Loan (APL) and/or Extended Term Insurance (ETI) after the transfer to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: Automatic Premium Loan and Extended Term Insurance are allowed to continue after the transfer of your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy to CPF Investment Scheme.

questions.question: Do I need to pay accrued interest if I used my CPF savings for CPF investments?
questions.answer: You do not need to pay back the accrued interest on the CPF savings used for your CPF investments.

questions.question: I work for an overseas employer outside Singapore and have to return to Singapore for personal reasons during the COVID-19 period. Are CPF contributions payable while I work remotely in Singapore?
questions.answer: If you are returning to Singapore for personal reasons and will be working remotely in Singapore for your overseas employer during the Stay Home Notice (SHN) period or unable to return overseas after your personal trip due to COVID-19 travel restrictions, CPF contributions are not payable until 30 June 2021 since this is a temporary work arrangement due to COVID-19 restrictions. However, similar to other employees who are working in Singapore, CPF contributions are payable on wages given to employees who are working remotely in Singapore from 1 July 2021 onwards.If you choose to continue working remotely in Singapore not due to COVID-19 travel restrictions, and your employer agrees with this work arrangement, CPF contributions are payable on your wages as they are given in respect of your employment in Singapore.

questions.question: If there are adjustments under CPF Investment Scheme in my Ordinary or Special Account, what interest rate will be used?
questions.answer: Any adjustments under the CPF Investment Scheme in your Ordinary or Special Account will be based on the CPF interest rates for the respective account. The interest rate will not include the extra 1% interest that is paid on the first $60,000 of your combined balances.

questions.question: Do I get tax relief for my voluntary top-up to my or my loved ones' MediSave Account?
questions.answer: When you make voluntary cash top-ups to (i) your MediSave Account or (ii) your loved ones, you can enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups made in each calendar year of up to:$ 8,000 if you make a top-up to yourself ; andan additional $ 8,000 if you make a cash top-up to your loved ones *.*Loved ones refer to parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, spouse and siblings.To qualify for tax relief for cash top-ups made to spouse/siblings, the recipient must (i) not have an annual income exceeding $8,0001in the year preceding the year of cash top-up (e.g. salary, tax exempt income such as bank interest, dividends and pension), or (ii) be handicapped.Please note the above tax relief cap applies to both voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account and Special/Retirement Account. You can find out more on theconditions to qualify for tax relief.1The income threshold for tax relief for cash top-ups to spouse or sibling has increased from $4,000 to $8,000 and will apply to cash top-ups made on 1 January 2024 or after.If you made a cash top-up to your spouse and/or sibling between 1 January 2024 and 16 February 2024 and wish to claim tax relief for the top-up made due to the increase in income threshold, you maysubmit an application to update your tax relief records for top-ups made in 2024.

questions.question: Why do I need to make other payment arrangements in order to renew my licence when I am already on Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.answer: Your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions are only based on an estimate of your MediSave payable for the current year. To renew your licence, you will need to pay your MediSave payable incurred in previous years via lump-sum payment(s) or monthly GIRO instalments.

questions.question: Will I receive Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions if I make a lump sum payment?
questions.answer: You will receive Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions of $20 monthly if you have contributed1at least $240 into your MediSave Account in the past 12 months.1You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person viaManage your MediSave payableorGIRO.

questions.question: What is the rationale of harmonising the criteria for new and existing funds under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: CPF Board ("CPFB") has, since 2006, taken measures to improve the quality of funds in CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) and lower the costs of investing. From 1 February 2006, new Unit Trusts and Investment-Linked Products (collectively known as "funds") must meet the stricter criteria1before being admitted into CPFIS2. From 1 January 2011, all funds in the CPFIS must meet the stricter criteria to continue to take in new CPF monies. This is part of CPFB's ongoing efforts to lower cost and improve the quality of CPFIS funds to benefit CPF members who seek to invest their CPF savings for higher returns.1(i) Top quartile of global peer group (ii) Total Expense Ratio lower than the median of CPFIS funds in respective risk class (iii) Sales charge not exceeding 3% and (iv) Preferably track record of 3 years.2Prior to 1 February 2006, the admission criterion was top 50 percentile of global peer group.

questions.question: I have received a notification on the refund of CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit but I have yet to receive my share of the excess contributions from my (ex-)employer, what should I do?
questions.answer: Your (ex-)employer has been notified to refund your share of excess CPF contributions to you, if any. You should contact your (ex-)employer directly regarding the refund.

questions.question: Why do I still need to contribute to MediSave even though I already have enough savings for my healthcare needs?
questions.answer: With rising healthcare costs, it is important to have enough savings for your healthcare needs. Contributing regularly to MediSave will help you build up your savings over your working life. These savings can help you meet your own as well as your loved ones’ hospitalisation expenses under unforeseen circumstances.

questions.question: I earn less than $500 per month. Do I qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: If you earn less than $500 per month, you will qualify for concessionary Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) if you belong to one of the groups and meet other WIS eligibility criteria:•            Person with Disability (PWD)•            Comcare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance recipient•            Caregiver of a care recipient. This generally includescaregiversresiding with care recipients who are medically certified to have permanent moderate to severe disabilities.For employees, you will receive a flat concessionary payment, based on age:Age in Work Year30 to 34 years35 to 44 years45 to 59 years60 years and above and all PWDsMonthly concessionary Workfare payment$50$75$120$130Self-employed persons (SEPs) will receive two-thirds of the WIS payments received by employees after they have made the required MediSave contributions.

questions.question: Can I transfer my CPF Investment Account under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account from one agent bank to another? If so, must I sell my investments first?
questions.answer: You may transfer your CPF Investment Account from one agent bank to another. You need not sell your investments, except for your investment in gold bought from your agent bank (excluding gold Exchange Traded Funds). All your investments and cash balances will be transferred along with your CPF Investment Account. To transfer your CPF Investment Account, you need to apply at the bank which you intend to transfer your account to.

questions.question: Do I need to inform my platform operator once I have opted in to increase my CPF contributions?
questions.answer: You do not need to inform your platform operator once you have opted in to increase your CPF contributions.Your platform operator will confirm your opt-in status with CPF Board directly.

questions.question: What are the conditions for applying to limit my MediSave payable as a self-employed person?
questions.answer: You can apply to limit your MediSave payable if your total employment income (excluding Additional Wages) for the year exceeds the maximum total annual income.Additional Wages are wage supplements which are not granted wholly and exclusively for the month. Examples are the annual bonus, leave pay, incentive and other payments made at intervals of more than a month.Please refer to the table below for the total employment income (excluding Additional Wages) that qualifies you to limit your MediSave contributions as a self-employed person.YearMaximum Total Annual Income(excluding Additional Wages)1993 - 2003$72,0002004$66,0002005$60,0002006 - 2010$54,0002011$56,0002012 - 2015$60,0002016 - 2022$72,0002023$73,2002024$81,6002025$88,8002026 onwards$96,000

questions.question: How do I receive my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support cash benefits via GovCash?
questions.answer: There are three options which you can choose to receive your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support cash benefits via GovCash:Option 1: Use LifeSG to transfer to PayNow-NRIC linked bank accountIf you have an existing bank account, you can link your account to PayNow-NRIC with your bank. Thereafter, login to LifeSG mobile app (LifeSG) using your Singpass to transfer your GovCash to your PayNow-NRIC linked bank account. The LifeSG app can be downloaded from the Apple App store or Google Play Store.Option 2: Use LifeSG for Scan & PayYou can use LifeSG to scan participating merchant’s QR code for purchases or scan your friend/family’s QR code to transfer your GovCash to them. You can only make purchases at merchants that accept PayNow/NETS QR code using the LifeSG app. You can look out for the PayNow/NETS logo on the SG QR label that is displayed by the merchants.Option 3: Withdraw from OCBC ATMsYou can withdraw your cash benefits at OCBC ATMs islandwide. You just need to enter:a) Your unique 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN)b) Your NRIC number; andc) pass the facial verificationYou do not need to have an OCBC bank account to use this service.You will receive the PRN via SMS or email after your cash benefits has been paid.You can also log into thee-serviceswith your Singpass to view your PRN by selecting “GovCash PRN” that is found at the menu on the left. This will only be available after the payment has been made.

questions.question: Why is there a need for the government to recover the excess Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) paid to workers?
questions.answer: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme supports lower-wage Singaporean workers’ income and retirement savings via cash and CPF contributions. To ensure that the WIS scheme remains fair, the excess WIS (both the cash and CPF portions) will be recovered from future WIS payment(s) that the worker may receive.For fraudulent cases, the recovery will be carried out immediately after the worker’s conviction or before conviction if the worker offered restitution in writing. Cash refund in lieu of CPF will be required if there are insufficient balances in the worker’s CPF accounts. Interest accrued on the outstanding cash amount may also be recovered. The worker will be issued aNotice to Attend Courtif the WIS payments are not refunded.

questions.question: With the closure of the Special Account and the raising of the Enhanced Retirement Sum, how much is the maximum amount that I can have in my Retirement Account?
questions.answer: From 1 January 2025, the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) was raised to four times of the Basic Retirement Sum to allow members 55 and above to save more in the Retirement Account (RA) andreceive higher payouts, if they wish to do so.With the change, the ERS in 2025 is $426,0001, up from $308,700 in 2024. Hence, if you are aged 55 and above in 2025, you can save up to $426,000 in the RA. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts of up to $3,300 for life from age 65 through CPF top-ups.Learn more about the payouts you can receive.As the ERS increases every January, you can make further top-ups every year for even higher payouts.1This is the limit for the savings set aside in the RA (excluding amounts such as interest earned, any government grants received, plus retirement withdrawals).

questions.question: When will my eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme be assessed and do I need to apply?
questions.answer: We will assess youreligibilityfor the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) annually at the beginning of the year. You do not need to apply.If you are eligible, we will notify you via email or post. You can also check your eligibility through theMRSS eligibility checker(no Singpass login required) andRetirement Dashboard.

questions.question: Who can make cash top-ups to recipients who are eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.answer: Anyone, including yourself,loved ones, employers or members of the community, can help members who are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to receive the matching grant by making cash top-ups to their Retirement Account.Learn more on how to make a cash top-uphere.

questions.question: I am renting a room/whole unit in the property that I stay in. Am I eligible for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: If you are renting the entire property unit, the annual value of that property unit will be used to assess your eligibility.If you are renting only a room or some rooms in the property, pleasewrite to uswith your tenancy agreement and particulars (name, NRIC, telephone number, address and the nature of your appeal).You can also write to us viaMailbox(Singpass required) and skip the hassle of keying in your personal particulars.We will review your WIS eligibility after we have received your request and the supporting documents.

questions.question: I have contributed up to the maximum mandatory contributions for the year. Do I still have to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.answer: If you’ve made Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions up to the maximum MediSave payable for the year, your applicable CAYE contribution rate will be 0%. This means that you will receive your service fee in full, and CAYE contribution will no longer be deducted from your service fee.However, you’ll still be required to make good your outstanding MediSave payable (if any) via lump-sum payment(s) or GIRO instalment plan.

questions.question: Can I use CPF savings to place Fixed Deposits under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: You can use your CPF savings to place Fixed Deposits (FD) with any of the four Fixed Deposit Banks (DBS, Maybank, OCBC and UOB) under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS). Currently, none of the FD banks are offering FD products under CPFIS.

questions.question: If I have terminated my insurance policy bought using CPF, can I reinstate the policy and pay the outstanding premiums and future premiums using CPF?
questions.answer: You need to liaise with your insurance company on the reinstatement of the policy. Upon reinstatement, you may pay the outstanding and future premiums using CPF. However, no CPF can be used to pay any outstanding interest owing to the insurance company.

questions.question: How much tax relief will I get for CPF contributions made as a platform worker?
questions.answer: If you are mandated or have opted in for increased CPF contributions:you will be allowed tax relief for your share of the mandatory CPF contributions. You will not have to pay tax on your platform operators’ share of mandatory CPF contributions.during the transitional period from 2025 to 2028, tax relief will also be allowed on voluntary CPF contributions to all three accounts, subject to a cap(based on the difference in the contribution rate in 2029, and at the contribution rate as at 31 December of the relevant year in which the voluntary contribution is made).once the mandatory CPF contribution rates have fully aligned with that for employees by 2029, only mandatory CPF contributions will be eligible for tax relief, similar to employees who do not enjoy tax relief for their voluntary CPF contributions to three CPF accounts.If you are not mandated and do not opt in for increased CPF contributions, you will enjoy the same tax relief as self-employed persons. If you make voluntary CPF contributions to all three CPF accounts, both your mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions will continue to be eligible for tax relief of up to 37% of your net trade income or $37,740, whichever is lower.Regardless of your opt-in status, you are eligible for CPF cash top-up relief if your platform operator makes cash top-ups on your behalf to your Retirement Account/ Special Account/ MediSave Account. This is aligned with the current treatment for employees.

questions.question: Do I need to pay additional fees due to trailer fees disclosure by my product/service providers? Is there any action required of me (as a CPFIS investor)?
questions.answer: You do not need to pay any additional fees. No action is required from you (as a CPFIS investor) given that trailer fees are paid by the fund manager or product provider to distributors.

questions.question: I am age 55 and above. How will the closure of Special Account (SA) affect my eligibility to voluntarily transfer my CPF savings to top up my own/loved ones' retirement savings?
questions.answer: There are no changes to the eligibility rules on the transfer of CPF savings to top up your own/loved ones' retirement savings.When your Special Account is closed, your withdrawable SA savings (if any) will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA), and your available CPF savings for such top-ups will increase accordingly. You can check these amounts available for such top-ups via the Retirement Dashboard, after we complete the closure of your SA in the second half of January 2025.

questions.question: I have made a top-up to my CPF accounts, do I still have to make MediSave contributions to offset my MediSave payable?
questions.answer: The contributions allocated to your MediSave Account via your top up to CPF accounts will not be used to offset your MediSave payable.If you want to make MediSave contributions to offset your outstanding (via instalment plan or full payment) or future MediSave payable, you may do so via theManage your MediSave Payableform.

questions.question: What will happen to my stock & gold investment limits arising from the merger of Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme and CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: Your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme stock & gold investment limits will be merged with your CPF Investment Scheme stock & gold investment limits.

questions.question: Will the funds that have already submitted their applications for inclusion under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) be affected by the revised criteria?
questions.answer: The revised criteria will only apply to fund applications received by the Board from 1 February 2006 onwards.

questions.question: What are the criteria for inclusion of Property Fund under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.answer: In considering the inclusion of Property Funds under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), the Board uses the following criteria:The property fund is offered by a company that is incorporated in Singapore;The property fund is listed on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) Mainboard;The property fund is traded in Singapore Dollars;The company allows Agent Banks to appoint all CPF unitholders of the property fund as proxies to attend and vote at meetings.You can refer to theSGX websitefor the list of Property Funds included under the CPFIS.

questions.question: Will I lose out on interest on my CPF contributions if my platform operator pays my CPF contributions late?
questions.answer: You will not lose out on the interest when your platform operator pays late. The interest will be credited to you when CPF Board recovers the CPF arrears from your platform operator.

questions.question: What actions do I need to take to file and claim tax relief for my cash top-up?
questions.answer: You do not need to file or claim tax relief for your cash top-up as we will automatically inform Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) if you have instructed to claim tax relief in your top-up application and are eligible.If you made a cash top-up to your spouse and/or sibling between 1 January 2024 and 16 February 2024 and wish to amend your instructions to claim tax relief for the top-up made due to the increase in income threshold from $4,000 to $8,000, you can refer tothis FAQ.Please note that only givers who make cash top-ups are eligible for tax relief. If you make cash top-ups to your loved ones, the tax relief does not apply to your receipients. Find outthe conditions to enjoy tax relief.

questions.question: If I do not opt in to increase my CPF contributions as a platform worker, will I be subject to the same CPF contribution rate as today?
questions.answer: The maximum CPF contribution rate for platform workers who do not opt in will remain at 8% to 10.5%, depending on their age and income. They will also only need to make MediSave contribution if they earn above $500 in a month from a platform.Some platform workers may see a difference in CPF contribution rate due to changes in the way CPF contribution is computed and collected. Today, platform workers’ earnings are aggregated across platforms and assessed annually when computing the applicable MediSave contribution. Moving forward, platform operators will be making CPF contribution on a monthly basis and based on earnings on each platform.CPF contribution rates are tiered based on income – a platform worker earning below $750 will have a lower CPF contribution rate. Overall, whether platform workers’ CPF contribution rate is lower or higher as compared to today depends on their individual circumstances. For example, if platform workers have multiple income streams from different platforms, and if their income for each platform is low, platform workers will be subject to the lower CPF contribution that is now applied on a per platform basis.

questions.question: What are the service standards for processing applications relating to discounted Singtel shares?
questions.answer: Please refer to the table for our service standards for processing applications relating to discounted Singtel shares.ServiceNormal Processing TimeWithdraw My Discounted Singtel Shares Upon Meeting CPF Withdrawal ConditionsWithin 15 working days(this includes the Central Depository's (CDP) processing time)Transfer Discounted Singtel Shares(Division of CPF-related Matrimonial Assets)Within 15 working days** Transferee must have a CPF investment account with agent bank

questions.question: From 2025, how are the matching grants and tax relief determined for my cash top-ups made to a senior eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.answer: From 1 January 2025, if you are making a cash top-up to a recipient eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS), your cash top-up of $2,000 will first enable your recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $2,000 per year from the Government, and will thus not be eligible for tax relief. You can continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for your cash top-ups that do not attract the MRSS matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).For example, if you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to your MRSS-eligible loved one, your loved one will first enjoy a matching grant of $2,000 from the Government, and you will be eligible for $1,000 of tax relief on your cash top-up that did not attract the matching grant.Find out more on theconditions to qualify for tax relief.

questions.question: I have applied to purchase Treasury Bills (T-bills) at primary auction under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS). When would my CPF savings be deducted for the purchase?
questions.answer: Your CPF savings for T-bills purchase under CPFIS would be deducted only upon the successful allotment of the T-bills. In so doing, CPF members will continue earning CPF interest on their CPF savings, in case full or part of their T-bills application is unsuccessful. The deductions are done after the auction date (i.e. the date where the allotment of your T-bills purchase has been finalised) but before the issue date of the T-bills.

questions.question: My employer does not pay my CPF. What can I do to qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: Under the CPF Act, employers must contribute CPF if their employees earn more than $50 a month, regardless of whether the employee is employed on a permanent, part-time, contract or casual basis.If your employer is not contributing CPF on your behalf, please approach your employer to clarify on the discrepancies. If your employer does not provide you with a satisfactory response, you can lodge a report with CPF Board.

questions.question: What benefits do self-employed persons enjoy from making MediSave contributions?
questions.answer: When you contribute to MediSave, you enjoy:Up to 6% interest1per annum on your MediSave savingsSavings in the MediSave Account earn 4% interest1per annum, and the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances earns an additional 1% interest per annum. Members aged 55 and above will also enjoy an additional 1% interest per annum on the first $30,000 of their combined CPF balance from 1 January 2016.Tax relief of up to 37% of your annual net trade income (NTI), the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740 or the actual amount contributed by you, whichever is lower. No tax relief is given if your assessed NTI for the year of assessment is zero or negative.Use of MediSave savingsto pay for a variety of medical expensesHassle-free licence application and renewalYou may also be eligible forWorkfare Income Supplement (WIS)payouts of up to $2,800 annually.1Based on the current 4% interest rate floor for MediSave savings. Refer toCPF interest ratesfor the current rates.

questions.question: I have just converted from a Singapore Permanent Resident to a Singapore Citizen. When should I apply the CPF contribution rates applicable to Singapore Citizens?
questions.answer: The CPF contribution rates for a Singapore Citizen will apply from the date you have converted to a Singapore Citizen.For Ordinary Wages (OW), your employer will need to pro-rate your OW and apply the appropriate rates to determine your CPF contributions. Your employer canwrite to usfor assistance on the computation if the OW for the month exceeds theOW ceilingor if the pro-rated wages are below $750.For Additional Wages (AW), your employer will need to apply the applicable contribution rate depending on when the AW is payable to you.Example:Assuming you are in your second year of Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status and become a Singapore Citizen on 15 June 2020:For OWThe second year SPR rate should be applied on the pro-rated wages for the period 1 June to 14 June 2020.The Singapore Citizen rate should be applied on the pro-rated wages for the period of 15 June to 30 June 2020.For AWThe second year SPR rate should be applied on the AW if it is payable between 1 June and 14 June 2020.The Singapore Citizen rate should be applied on the AW if it is payable between 15 June and 30 June 2020.

questions.question: I plan to top up my Retirement Account to the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum. When can I make the top-up?
questions.answer: You can make your top-up anytime from 1 January 2025 onwards, once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.Find outhow you can check the amount that you can top up.

questions.question: I am a contract / part-time employee. Will I be eligible for Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.answer: Contract / part-time employees are eligible for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) if they meet theWIS eligibility criteria.

questions.question: Where can I find a copy of the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Profits/Losses Report?
questions.answer: Please refer to theCPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Profits/Losses Report.

questions.question: I am currently holding investments under the CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA). Do I need to do anything?
questions.answer: You do not need to take any immediate action. You can continue to hold your existing CPFIS-SA investments until you decide to sell them or until they mature.You can view your SA Portfolio by logging in tomy cpf digital serviceswith your Singpass > Select my cpf > My dashboards > Investment.

questions.question: How is members' investment performance in the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.answer: Please refer to theCPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) Profits/Losses Reportif you wish to view members' investment performance in the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA).

questions.question: How do I use my CPF to apply for shares, property funds or corporate bonds offered during an Initial Public Offering (IPO) under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.answer: You may apply for the IPO in any of the available ways.Use your agent bank's ATMs for your application;Use your agent bank's internet banking for your application; orObtain a CPF cashier's order from your agent bank's counter and attach it to your IPO application form.The amount of CPF needed will be transferred automatically from your Ordinary Account to your CPF Investment Account.

questions.question: Does the CPF annual ceiling apply to my net earnings as a platform worker?
questions.answer: Yes, you will be subject to the same CPF annual ceiling of $102,000 as employees. You do not need to make any CPF contributions on net earnings exceeding $102,000 in a year.As CPF contributions are computed separately for each platform operator you work with, this annual ceiling applies on a per-platform basis.If your total net earnings for the year across all platforms have exceeded CPF annual ceiling of $102,000, you canapply for a refundon your share of the contributions.

questions.question: Why are platform workers above a certain age not eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is intended to offset part of the year-on-year increase in a platform worker’s own share of CPF contributions to his Ordinary and Special accounts, during the phase-in period when platform workers’ CPF contribution rates are gradually increased to align with employees’.Platform workers who do not see an increase in their share of CPF contributions will not receive PCTS as there is no increase in CPF contributions to offset.This includes platform workers aged above 65 who opt in, as they will see a reduction in their own share of CPF contributions . As they will not see a drop in their take-home pay due to the decision to opt in, they will not receive PCTS.In 2025, platform workers aged above 60 to 65 will also not see an increase in their own share of CPF contributions and thus they will not be eligible.For platform workers in these age groups, although there is a reduction in their own share of CPF contributions after opting in, their total CPF contributions will still increase, after taking into account the platform operator’s CPF contributions.

questions.question: Can I continue to use my CPF monies to pay for the quarterly bank charges even if I do not have $20,000 in my Ordinary Account?
questions.answer: You can use your Ordinary Account balance to pay for the quarterly agent banks charges, even if your Ordinary Account balance is below $20,000. The restriction on the use of the first $20,000 in Ordinary Account for CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account only applies to new investments, including payments for recurring single premiums (for insurance) and regular savings plans (for unit trusts).

questions.question: How do I declare my annual net trade income online as a self-employed person?
questions.answer: For Work Year 2023 (WY2023) onwardsAll Net Trade Income (NTI) declarations for Work Year 2023 (Year of Assessment 2024) can be made with the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) by filing a tax return. There is no need to file separate declarations with CPF Board.If you receive a notification (via letter/form/SMS) to file tax from IRAS or you meet the requirement to file tax (i.e. NTI above $6,000 and/or Total Income above $22,000), please complete and submit the tax return to IRAS directly. The income tax filing period is from 1 March to 18 April annually.If you do not receive a notification from IRAS or do not meet the requirement to file tax, you can declare your self-employed net trade income (NTI) to IRAS viamyTax Portalwhich will be available from 1 March to 31 October annually for taxpayers to e-File tax returns.Once IRAS has assessed your income for the year, your assessed NTI will be transmitted to the Board. You can check your updated NTI records by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard with your Singpass.For Work Year 2022 (WY2022) or earlierIf you were not issued a Notice of Assessment (NOA) by IRAS and wish to declare NTI for work years prior to 2023, you canwrite to ususing your Singpass.If you have declared your NTI with IRAS, you need not declare your income again to CPF Board.

questions.question: Why do I need to open a CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account now to 'hold' my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Investment?
questions.answer: The Academic Staff Provident Fund (ASPF) Part V Scheme does not fall under the purview of the ASPF Investment Scheme. Under the ASPF Part V Scheme, the policies were bought under the name of National University Singapore (NUS). NUS had been paying the premiums directly to the insurance companies, after deducting the monies from members' ASPF Ordinary Accounts, without going through the agent banks. As the CPF Board does not have such a scheme, Part V insurance policies have to be transferred to the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) instead. Under the CPFIS-OA, you need to have a CPFIS Investment Account to hold your investments, including the transferred Part V insurance policies.

questions.question: What is the personal income tax relief cap and why is there a cap on this relief for cash top-ups made?
questions.answer: Thepersonal income tax relief capsets a limit on the total amount of tax relief you can claim.Even though each relief serves a good purpose, some individuals may end up with a significantly reduced taxable income when multiple reliefs are combined. Therefore, tax relief on cash top-ups is also subjected to the personal income tax relief cap.

questions.question: Why are cash top-ups beyond Full Retirement Sum not eligible for tax relief?
questions.answer: Givers enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups up to the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This is in line with the intent of tax relief benefits to encourage cash top-ups to members with lower to average CPF retirement balances.

questions.question: My mobile number is already registered to my bank account on PayNow. Can the Government credit my Government cash benefits to me via PayNow-Mobile instead of via PayNow-NRIC?
questions.answer: We can only credit your Government cash benefits to you via your PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account. NRIC is an unchanged proxy issued by the Government, compared to mobile numbers which may be easily changed. To ensure that the money is credited to the correct recipient’s bank account, only NRIC will be accepted as the proxy for Government benefits via PayNow.Eligible seniors who have linked their NRIC to PayNow, with a PayNow-GIRO-participating bank will receive the benefits in this bank account.

questions.question: How does CPF Board currently assess whether funds admitted are still suitable to remain in CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.answer: When determining if a product is suitable to be under CPF Investment Scheme, the emphasis so far has been on past performance and the competency of its investment professionals. Re-evaluation will be required for Fund Management Companies/Funds that have undergone material changes in the organisational structure, fund structure or management team.

questions.question: What proportion of funds applying for admission into CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) has been successful? What is the target under the revised criteria?
questions.answer: Fund managers would generally assess the quality of their funds using the published CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) evaluation criteria before applying for inclusion under CPFIS. Thus far, funds within the top 50 percentile in their global peer group1have been successful in their application for admission into CPFIS, and the majority of funds that have applied for admission into CPFIS have been admitted.New funds will need to meet a higher criterion - i.e. they must be among the top 25 percentile of funds. Going forward, we do not expect a significant change in the success rate of application as managers would continue to assess the quality of their funds against the CPFIS evaluation criteria before application.1This refers to comparison of funds of similar asset class/strategy on a world-wide basis.

questions.question: If I wish to make both a CPF transfer and a cash top-up to myself / my loved one, which should I do first?
questions.answer: If you wish to enjoy tax relief on your cash top-up to help you or your loved one up to the Full Retirement Sum, please make the cash top-up first, before the CPF transfer. If you prefer using your CPF savings over cash, please make the CPF transfer first.You may wish to take note that only cash top-ups to self and loved ones within the Full Retirement Sum can enjoy tax relief. Learn more abouttax relief.

questions.question: Where will proceeds from my CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA) investments go to after my Special Account has been closed?
questions.answer: After yourSpecial Account has been closed, the proceeds from your CPFIS-SA investments will be paid to your Retirement Account up to your Full Retirement Sum, with any remaining balance paid to your Ordinary Account.

questions.question: How can I update my contact details to receive notification on my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.answer: To receive notification via SMS or email on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment, you may update your mobile number viamy cpfdigital services -Account Settingswith your Singpass.

questions.question: I have a partnership firm. Do all partners need to make MediSave contributions before renewing the business licence?
questions.answer: All partners (if they derive trade income) must fulfil their MediSave payable before the business licence can be renewed.

questions.question: How will the proceeds of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy and/or rider be distributed?
questions.answer: In general, premiums of Part V insurance policies and riders (if any) paid using Academic Staff Provident Fund (ASPF) monies or cash prior to the transfer of the policy to CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) would be treated as though the premiums were paid using CPF monies. This is because Section 22 of the First Schedule of the National University Singapore (Corporatisation) Act provides that all premiums paid or deemed to have been paid with ASPF moneys in respect of ASPF Approved Investment Scheme Investments and Part V Assurances shall, on and after the dissolution date, be deemed to have been paid with CPF monies. Hence, the proportion of the proceeds (except death benefits) corresponding to such premiums would be refunded to your CPFIS Investment Account.However, the distribution of the full proceeds would depend on the premium payment mode after the transfer of the Part V policy to CPFIS. If, after the transfer of your policy to CPFIS:All the premiums of your Part V insurance policy and rider are paid using your CPF Ordinary Account savingsIf all the premiums of your Part V insurance policy and rider are paid using your CPF Ordinary Account savings, all proceeds would have to be refunded to your CPFIS Investment Account.Your CPF monies are exhausted and you then use cash to pay the premiums of the Part V insurance policy and riderIf your CPF monies are exhausted and you used cash to pay the premiums of the Part V insurance policy and rider, the proceeds would be pro-rated based on CPF savings vis-à-vis cash used to pay for the premiums after the transfer. The CPF portion and cash portion of the proceeds will be respectively refunded to your CPFIS Investment Account and to you.All the premiums of the Part V insurance policy and rider are paid using cashIf all the premiums of the Part V insurance policy and rider are paid using cash, the proportion of the proceeds corresponding to the premiums paid in cash after the transfer of the policy to CPFIS would be refunded to you in cash. The remaining proceeds would be refunded to your CPFIS Investment Account.

questions.question: Can my platform operator’s contributions be used to offset outstanding MediSave contributions from my past self-employed work?
questions.answer: Your CPF contributions (including platform operator’s share, if any) are meant for platform work done from 2025.You will need to make separate arrangements to settle any outstanding MediSave contributions on past income earned as a self-employed person.You may reach out to CPFB to arrange affordableinstalment planson your past MediSave obligations.

questions.question: Will I receive any notifications after the transfer of my investments from my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: You will receive a letter from your agent bank, informing you of the details of the investments being transferred from your Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Investment Account to your CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) Investment Account. You will also receive a letter from National University of Singapore after the transfer.You can also view your Special Account (SA) investment holdings (combination of ASPFAIS-SA and CPFIS-SA) in your SA portfolio statement anytime using your Singpass viamy cpfdigital services.

questions.question: Who do I contact for further details on my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and net service fee payment amount?
questions.answer: To view your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and other payment details, you may log in to theSelf-employment dashboardusing your Singpass, underContribute As You Earn > Show all payments. You can alsocontact us through these channels.For more details on the net service fee, please contact the company or agency you have contracted with directly. If there are any non-payment, short payment or late payment of service fees, you may wish to take up the dispute directly with your buyer and seek mediation through theTripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM)or other industry facilitated mediation services.

questions.question: Will the estimated income that I have provided for the computation of my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate be used as the income to compute my MediSave payable for the year?
questions.answer: The income information you provided for Contribute As You Earn  (CAYE) is only used to compute the CAYE contribution rate. It will not be used as your actual income to compute your MediSave payable for the year.You’ll still need to declare your Net Trade Income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) or CPF Board the following year. Your MediSave payable for the year will then be computed based on that NTI.

questions.question: When will the top-ups received in my CPF Special/Retirement Account start to earn interest?
questions.answer: If you receive a cash top-up this month, it will start earning interest in the next month.For CPF transfers of existing CPF savings, you will start earning interest in your account from this month. However, if the CPF savings are fresh injections, it will start earning interest in your account from the next month.

questions.question: Why do I still need to declare my income to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS)/ CPF Board when I have already done so on Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services?
questions.answer: The revenue and expenses information on the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is an estimate of your business outlook for the year and used only to compute your CAYE contribution rate. It is not a declaration of your actual Net Trade Income (NTI) and you are still required to declare your actual NTI in the following year to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) / CPF Board to compute your mandatory MediSave payable.

questions.question: I am 55, can I transfer my Ordinary Account savings to my Special Account to earn a higher interest rate?
questions.answer: No, you will not be able to make CPF transfers to your Special Account (SA) after you turn 55. Instead, your transfers will be made to your Retirement Account (RA), which was created for your retirement needs.Did you know?If you wish to earn higherintereston your Ordinary Account (OA) savings (which earns at least 2.5% interest* per annum) and boost your monthly payouts, you canmake a CPF transferto your RA (which earns at least 4% interest* per annum), up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum. Do note that for CPF transfers to RA, your SA savings (if any) will be transferred first followed by your OA savings.* Based on the current interest rate floor on Ordinary and Retirement Account monies.

questions.question: Can I purchase a regular premium insurance policy under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: With effect from 1 January 2001, CPF savings cannot be used for new regular premium insurance policies. Only Single Premium or Recurring Single Premium insurance policy is allowed under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account and CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account.

questions.question: I have made a voluntary refund. Do I still need to refund to my CPF account when I sell my property?
questions.answer: The amount that you have to refund upon selling your property depends on how much you have voluntarily refunded:If you have fully refunded all the CPF savings you have withdrawn for your property with accrued interest, you do not need to make any refundsIf you have partially refunded the CPF savings you have withdrawn for your property with accrued interest, you will need to refund the balance CPF savings you have used with interestWhen a property is sold, the selling price will generally will be used to pay the following in this order:1. Outstanding housing loan2. Required CPF refund3. Other sale expenses, e.g., legal fees;If the selling price (including the option monies) after paying the outstanding housing loan is not enough to make the required CPF refund, you do not need to top up the shortfall in cash as long as the property is sold at market value.However, the option monies (e.g. option fee and option exercise fee) received from your buyer in cash upon the sale of your property are considered part of the selling price and need to be refunded to your co-owner’s and your CPF accounts before the transaction can be completed.The refunded amount will be returned to your co-owner's and your CPF accounts in the following proportions:Amount returned to owner A’s CPF Account:Amount returned to owner B’s CPF Account:

questions.question: Do residents in welfare homes qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: Residents in welfare homes registered with the National Council of Social Service/ Ministry of Health/ Ministry of Social and Family Development will qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) if they meet all of the otherWIS eligibility criteria.

questions.question: I have made the required MediSave contribution to qualify for Workfare Income Supplement, why is my payment still not reflected in the MediSave Payable page after logging into e-Services?
questions.answer: Contributions made each month will be updated in e-Services on the 9th working day of the following month.

questions.question: What is the increase in platform workers’ share of CPF Ordinary and Special Account contribution rates, which is used to compute Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: From 2025 to 2028, platform workers’ own share of CPF contributions rates will increase by up to 2.5%-points each year, until it reaches up to 20% in 2029, to align with employees. This applies to platform workers born in or after 1995, or born before 1995 and opted in to increased CPF contributions (see illustration for example).Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) will offset a percentage of this year-on-year increase of up to 2.5%-points in contribution rate. The offset percentage will taper down from 2025 to 2028. In 2029, when platform workers’ CPF contributions are completely aligned with that of employees, PCTS will cease.*Infographic shows CPF contribution rates for platform workers in the “35 & below” age group, with net earnings above $750 in a month.

questions.question: Can I choose to continue to submit my bank account details to receive payments for government service instead of PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address), and what do I need to do to ensure I can continue to receive my service fee payments?
questions.answer: You will only be able to use the bank account registered to your PayNow to receive service fee payments.Please ensure that you have registered for PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) so that you receive your service fee payments promptly.
