If not, you will not be able to receive your service fee payments from early June 2024.We encourage you to check with your bank to ensure your details are updated or if you need more information on how to sign up for PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address).

questions.question: Why is it mandatory for platform workers born in 1995 or later to have increased CPF contributions aligned to employees, while those born before 1995 have the option to opt in?
questions.answer: Younger platform workers have a greater need for CPF contributions because of housing needs and can benefit more from the compounding interest given their longer runway for accumulation.Older platform workers can choose to opt in to the increased CPF contributions if they wish to, as they may have existing plans to finance housing and retirement needs.Older platform workers who do not opt in will continue to be required to make CPF MediSave contributions, and will not receive the platform operator’s share of CPF contributions.Platform operators will deduct the CPF contributions from platform workers’ earnings as and when they earn and transmit them to CPF Board monthly for all platform workers, including the MediSave contributions for those who do not opt in.

questions.question: How can I update or terminate my GIRO bank account for recurring cash top-ups?
questions.answer: You canupdateyour GIRO bank account for your recurring cash top-up bysetting up a new GIRO arrangement. If you have existing recurring top-up arrangements, the deductions could still be from your previous GIRO bank account for the current month.Find out more.You canterminateyour GIRO arrangement for your recurring cash top-up by submittingthis form. All monthly and/or yearly GIRO deductions for top-ups to your recipient(s) will cease.

questions.question: I have substantial balances in my Ordinary and Special Accounts. Can I use the available funds to offset my MediSave payable?
questions.answer: The three CPF accounts, Ordinary, Special and MediSave Accounts, serve different purposes. While Ordinary and Special Account savings are meant for retirement, your MediSave Account savings are for your healthcare needs. Thus, the balances in your Ordinary and Special accounts cannot be used to settle your MediSave payable.

questions.question: What if I am in financial hardship and is unable to set aside monies for MediSave via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme?
questions.answer: We understand that some self-employed persons (SEPs) may be facing financial difficulties and may not be able to cope with Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). Thus, if you do not have outstanding MediSave payable or are contributing via GIRO instalments, you may set your CAYE contribution rate to 0%. This means that you’ll receive your service payment in full, and CAYE contribution will not be deducted from your service payment. Pleasewrite to usif you wish to apply for a 0% CAYE contribution rate. CPF Board will assess your eligibility and inform you of the outcome in writing.

questions.question: Can taxi principal hirers who are not liable to make a MediSave contribution qualify for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution from their taxi operators?
questions.answer: Taxi principal hirers who do not have outstanding MediSave payable can still receive Drive and Save co-contributions if they make contributions to pre-pay their future MediSave payable1:A contribution of at least $20 to their MediSave Account monthly, orA lump sum MediSave contribution of at least $240 in the past 12 months.1Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions to pre-pay their MediSave payable as self-employed persons viaManage your MediSave payable.

questions.question: How is my net trade income determined for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) if I am a self-employed person?
questions.answer: From Work Year 2023 onwards, all Net Trade Income (NTI) declarations must be made with Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). The Workfare Income Supplement you are eligible to receive will be computed based on your NTI earned in the Work Year (not including previous years’ losses) that CPF Board receives from IRAS.

questions.question: I am eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme this year. Will I still be eligible if there are changes to my circumstance during the year?
questions.answer: Yes, you will still be eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for the year even if your circumstances change (e.g. increase in monthly income) during the year. Your eligibility for MRSS will be assessed next year based on your new circumstances.However, do note that renouncing your Singapore citizenship during the year will make you ineligible for the scheme and matching grant.Find out about theconditions which you need to meetto receive and keep the matching grant.

questions.question: I received Matched Retirement Savings Scheme matching grants in the past, before the $20,000 lifetime cap took effect in 2025. Will the past matching grants count towards this $20,000 lifetime cap?
questions.answer: The lifetime cap will only be applied from 2025 onwards. Matching grants received in the past for cash top-ups made prior to 2025, will not count towards the $20,000 lifetime cap.

questions.question: Do I still have to contribute to MediSave as a self-employed person even though my MediSave balance has reached the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.answer: As a self-employed person (SEP), you are still required to make MediSave contributions even if you have met the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). This is the same for employees.The MediSave amount above the BHS will be transferred to your CPF Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA), which have interest rates equal or higher than that of the MediSave Account. The BHS cap and overflow arrangement are intentionally planned to avoid over savings in MediSave and to supplement your retirement savings. These overflows which end up in your SA or RA can be withdrawn according to the withdrawal guidelines. For members who have met the Full Retirement Sum in their SA or RA, the savings in excess of the BHS will be transferred to the Ordinary Account (OA). Savings in the OA can be used for other purposes such as housing repayment.

questions.question: What will happen to my CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments if I leave Singapore permanently and withdraw all my CPF monies?
questions.answer: For CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA), we will inform the agent bank to close your CPF Investment Account. The agent bank will contact you for the withdrawal of your investments and cash balance (if any) in your CPF Investment Account. Your investments will be transferred* to your own name and you may thereafter continue servicing your investments using cash or liquidate them as you wish and have the sale proceeds paid to you directly.* Central Depository (Pte) Ltd (“CDP”) imposes a transfer fee of $10.00 (excluding GST) for every share counter transferred from your CPF Investment Account to your CDP Account.For CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA), we will inform your product provider(s) to transfer your investments to your own name and you may thereafter liquidate them as you wish and have the sale proceeds paid to you directly.Once withdrawn, your CPFIS investments and cash balance in your CPF Investment Account will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.

questions.question: Why must self-employed persons (SEPs) contribute to MediSave to receive Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: A key principle of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is that each recipient has a personal responsibility to save for his future needs, with the government providing additional support.Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required to contribute to their MediSave Accounts as they do not receive regular MediSave contributions from employers. It is important to contribute regularly to ensure enough savings for healthcare needs. This is especially important during old age, when SEPs may have stopped working.WIS is intended to supplement, not replace the MediSave contributions made by the SEPs.

questions.question: I do not have outstanding MediSave payable as a self-employed person. Can I make MediSave contributions to offset my future payables?
questions.answer: You may make MediSave contributions to offset your future payables, up to the prevailing CPF Annual Limit.The total CPF contributions (voluntary and mandatory CPF contributions) made for the calendar year should not exceed the prevailing CPF Annual Limit. Any contributions made in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded without interest.The Board must receive the MediSave contributions by the last working day of the year for them to be counted towards the year’s CPF Annual Limit. Backdating of MediSave contributions to previous years is not allowed.You can enjoytax reliefon your MediSave contributions, if eligible, based on your annual net trade income.

questions.question: What are the criteria for inclusion of Fixed Deposit Banks under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.answer: In considering the inclusion of Fixed Deposit Banks under CPF Investment Scheme, the Board uses the following criteria:The bank must be locally incorporated with minimum capital funds of S$1.5 billion and good credit rating; orThe bank must be a subsidiary of a locally-incorporated bank which meets the criteria at (i). The bank must continue to be a subsidiary of the locally-incorporated bank; orIf the bank is a foreign bank, it must be accorded the Qualifying Full Bank privileges.

questions.question: Am I eligible for tax reliefs when I make a cash top-up to my/my loved ones' retirement savings?
questions.answer: You can enjoy tax relief if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident and make cash top-ups*within the current year’s Full Retirement Sum for yourself, yourloved ones, employees or platform workers.Find out more aboutthe amount of tax relief you can enjoy.Find out more on theconditions to qualify for tax relief.*From 1 January 2025, givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $2,000 per year) under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will no longer receive tax relief. Find out more onhow this works.

questions.question: I have just obtained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. Do I need to contribute CPF?
questions.answer: Yes, CPF contributions are payable from the day you obtained your Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status.In the first two years of obtaining the SPR status, you and your employer will contribute to CPF at graduated rates to help you adjust to the lower take-home pay. However, you and your employer have the option toapply jointly to CPF Board to contribute at higher rates.

questions.question: What is the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS) enhancement that applies to platform workers?
questions.answer: Eligible platform workers who are mandated or opt in to the increased CPF contributions will receive higher Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS) payments at the same level as employees from 2029, once their CPF contribution rates fully align with that of employees. They will also receive a higher proportion of WIS payments in cash – 40% compared to 10% today.All eligible platform workers will also receive WIS monthly (instead of annually) from March 2025. This is because platform operators will deduct CPF contributions from platform workers as and when they earn and submit them to CPF Board every month from 2025 onwards, including MediSave contributions for those who do not opt in.

questions.question: Will all my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V Insurance Policies be transferred to CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: All your Part V insurance policies will be transferred to your CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account with the agent bank.

questions.question: Can I make the top-up by cash or NETS under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.answer: No, you can use PayNow or GIRO instead to make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ Retirement Account (RA).For PayNow, your cash top-up will generally be credited almost instantly upon successful payment.Consider making regular monthly or yearly cash top-ups conveniently via GIRO, without the hassle of completing the application form every time you top up.You may refer to this FAQ“How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?”for the guide on how to top up.

questions.question: Why are my current discounted Singtel shareholdings different from the quantity I purchased in 1993 and/or 1996 even though I did not sell the shares?
questions.answer: Singtel performed capital reductions on 1 September 2004 and 1 September 2006. In the 2004 capital reduction, Singtel cancelled 1 in every 14 of its shares, with the resultant shareholding rounded-up to the nearest 10 shares, where applicable. Singtel then reimbursed you S$2.36 for each cancelled share. In the 2006 capital reduction, Singtel cancelled 1 in every 20 of its shares, with the resultant shareholding rounded-up to the nearest 10 shares, where applicable. Singtel reimbursed you $2.74 for each cancelled share. Both reimbursements were credited into your CPF Ordinary Account. You were then informed, in writing, of the capital reductions in September 2004 and September 2006.

questions.question: If I run out of CPF monies to pay the premiums of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policies, what should I do?
questions.answer: You have the following options:Use cash to pay the premiums;Convert your Part V insurance policies to a paid-up mode1; orActivate the Automatic Premium Loan (APL)2or Extended Term Insurance (ETI)3feature(s) of your Part V insurance policies, if they have such features and if your insurance company allows you to do so.1Converting a policy to paid-up mode means that the policyholder will not need to pay premiums anymore. The sum assured of a paid-up policy is usually lower than that of the original policy. All supplementary riders attached will be terminated.2APL means that once the policy has accumulated sufficient cash value, if the policyholder is unable to pay the premium, he can borrow from the cash value. However, he is required to pay back the loan and compound interest. Once the loan plus compound interest exceeds the cash value of the policy, the policy will lapse.3ETI means that if the policyholder still wants the insurance protection but doesn't want to pay any more premiums, the existing cash value of his policy is treated as a single premium which is used to buy protection for future years. The number of years of protection he will get varies directly with the quantum of the cash value.

questions.question: Can I increase or decrease the premiums to be paid for my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policies?
questions.answer: Academic Staff Provident Fund (ASPF) members are not allowed to make any changes to their Part V insurance policies that will cause anincreasein premiums with effect from 28 December 2006 (i.e. the date that National University Singapore issued the official "Dissolution Notice" to all its members). However, if the increase in premiums is due to attained age at renewal of the policies1, or conversion of the policies2, you can use your CPF monies to pay the higher premium.ASPF members can make any changes to their Part V insurance policies that will result in adecreasein premiums, as long as the insurance companies allow it.1When a member exceeds a certain age, he may have to pay a higher premium to renew his insurance policy. In such an instance, he can continue to use his CPF monies to pay the higher premiums.2A member's insurance policy contract may allow him to convert: (1) a rider to a new whole life policy, endowment policy or investment-linked insurance product (ILP); or (2) a whole life policy to an endowment policy or vice versa.

questions.question: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), how much MediSave contribution would I have to make from my service fee?
questions.answer: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), the amount of MediSave contribution deducted from your service fee is based on your estimated annual revenue and expenses for the year.Your CAYE contribution rate is determined by the following formula:CAYE contribution rate =(A x B) / CwhereAis the MediSave contribution rate for your estimated annual Net Trade Income (NTI)1and age for the year;Bis your estimated annual NTI1for the year2; andCis your estimated annual revenue for the year21Your estimated annual NTI is derived using your estimated annual revenue less estimated annual expenses for the year.2If you did not provide your estimated annual revenue and expenses for the year, it will be based on your actual revenue and expenses assessed by IRAS two years ago.A floor CAYE contribution rate of 2% will apply if you have earned more than $6,000 two years ago.To ensure that your CAYE contribution rate reflects your business outlook for the year accurately, please estimate your revenue and expenses by logging in to theSelf-employment dashboardusing your Singpass, underContribute As You Earn > Update contribution rate. You can adjust your CAYE contribution rate as and when there are changes to your estimated revenue and expenses. Generally, your updated rate will apply to payments made from the next day.Otherwise, a personalised default CAYE contribution rate computed based on your NTI assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) two years ago will apply.Example on how the CAYE contribution rate will be computed

questions.question: What are the criteria for inclusion of Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.answer: In considering the inclusion of Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), the Board uses the following criteria:The gold ETF is backed by physical gold that meets the London Good Delivery Rules issued by London Bullion Market Association (or other equivalent globally accepted standards);The gold ETF is offered by a Singapore-incorporated company (for locally constituted gold ETF authorized by MAS) or through a local representative (for foreign gold ETF recognized by MAS);The gold ETF is listed on the SGX; andThe company allows Agent Banks to appoint all CPF unitholders of the gold ETF as proxies to attend and vote at meetings.What are the criteria for a local representative to offer foreign Gold ETF?The criteria for a local representative to offer foreign Gold ETF are:Must be a company incorporated in Singapore;Must provide CPF Board a copy of the representative agreement evidencing the appointment of the representative by the foreign gold ETF issuer or marketing agent;Provide evidence of indemnity mechanism (such as back-to-back agreement) put in place between the representative and the foreign issuer/marketing agent, allowing the representative to have recourse to the foreign issuer/marketing agent if the latter does not discharge its duties, obligations and responsibilities with due care and in good faith;Have good regulatory compliance record in Singapore; andHave sound financial position.Which Gold ETFs are included under the CPFIS?List of Gold ETFs included under the CPFIS:SPDR Gold Shares (under SGX trading name "GLD US$" and "GLD SG$")

questions.question: How can I provide or update my mobile number to receive SMS notification on my Workfare payment?
questions.answer: We will only send SMS notifications on Workfare payments to the mobile number that you have registered with CPF Board.To receive SMS notifications, you may update your mobile number viamy cpfdigital services -Account Settingswith your Singpass.

questions.question: How will I know whether the funds that I am holding under the CPF Investment Scheme do not meet the stricter criteria by December 2010?
questions.answer: If the funds do not meet the stricter criteria by December 2010, the respective Fund Management Company(FMC)/insurer will be required to inform their CPF clients in writing, and to offer their clients three options, by December 2010.

questions.question: How much cash and CPF contributions will I receive from the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme?
questions.answer: If you are an employee, you will receive 60% of your Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) in CPF contributions and the remaining 40% in cash.A higher proportion is credited into your Special/Retirement and MediSave Accounts to boost your retirement and healthcare savings, as savings in these accounts earn up to 5% per annum if you are below 55, and up to 6% per annum if you are 55 or above.You can refer to the table below on the allocation of the WIS CPF into the three accounts, according to the age bands*.Age(Years)Ordinary AccountMediSave AccountSpecial/Retirement Account35 & below30%35%35%Above 35 - 4529%37%34%Above 45 – 5028%38%34%Above 50 – 5525%38%38%Above 55 – 6043%45%11%Above 60 – 6521%64%15%Above 658%84%8%If you are a self-employed person, you will receive 90% of your WIS in your MediSave Account and the remaining 10% in cash.* Figures may not add up due to rounding.

questions.question: After the merger of Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) and CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), will the transfer be reflected in any of my CPFIS statements?
questions.answer: The transfer will be reflected through the change tothe net amount withdrawn.  Your net amount withdrawn under the Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (ASPFAIS-OA) will be merged with your net amount withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA).  A footnote will be permanently shown in your "CPFIS Stock & Gold Limits Computation" statement, informing you of the amount transferred from your ASPFAIS-OA. For your investments made under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme -Special Account (ASPFAIS-SA), they will be transferred to your CPF Investment Scheme - Special Account (CPFIS-SA). You are able to view your combined investment holdings in your SA portfolio statement.

questions.question: When can I receive my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments and which bank account will my PCTS payments be credited to?
questions.answer: As an eligible platform worker, you will receive Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment in cash every month. The table below shows when you will receive the payments.You will receive the PCTS in your bank account or via GovCashFor work done inPayNow – NRIC / Bank CreditingGovCashJanEnd March1stweek of AprilFebEnd April1stweek of MayMarEnd May1stweek of JuneMonth XEnd of month (X + 2)1stweek of the following month (X + 3)You will receive the PCTS payment via your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account. To check your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account details, please approach your bank.If you do not have a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account but provided your DBS/POSB, OCBC or UOB bank account to the Government previously, your PCTS will be credited to the bank account that you have registered to receive Government benefits. You may use thislinkto provide or update your bank account details*.If you do not have a registered or PayNow NRIC-linked bank account, you will receive PCTS via GovCash later in the 1stweek of the following month, as opposed to using PayNow-NRIC or Bank Crediting.*If you have linked your NRIC number to your bank account or submitted your bank account details after the 14thof the month, your updates will only be effective in the following month.

questions.question: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if I am below 55 years old?
questions.answer: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) helps boost the retirement payouts of older Singaporean Citizens aged 55 and above with lower retirement savings, who have a shorter runway to build up more retirement savings. MRSS is extended to them to help accumulate retirement savings.For those who are younger and have a longer runway to build their retirement savings, the Government provides various other support. These include the Workfare Income Supplement, which supplements the income and retirement savings of lower-wage workers, and the Retirement Sum Topping-Up scheme (RSTU), which provide tax relief on cash top-ups. These schemes boost retirement savings, allowing members to benefit from compounding interest and higher monthly payouts in retirement.

questions.question: Will I receive a notification informing me that my CPF contributions have been credited by my platform operators?
questions.answer: Yes, you will receive a CPF Contribution Alert. The CPF Contribution Alert is a notification service to inform CPF members, including platform workers, when their monthly CPF contributions are credited. For example, you will be notified when your CPF contributions for the month of March 2025 have been credited any day between 1 March 2025 to 30 April 2025.CPF members can receive the notification via:their registeredemail address; orpush notification via CPF Mobile app. CPF members will need toenable personalised notificationswithin the mobile app’s settings to start receiving the Alert.With the CPF Contribution Alert, you can conveniently verify the CPF contributions paid by your platform operator against your earnings slip.If there are any discrepancies or if you have any clarifications, please approach your platform operator immediately so that any error can be rectified early while documentary evidence is fresh. If CPF contributions were paid in error, your platform operator will need to submit an adjustment or refund request immediately, and no later than one year from the payment date.Find outmore information on the CPF Contribution Alert.

questions.question: I have already contributed up to the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). Why am I still required to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.answer: As a self-employed person, you’re still required to make MediSave contributions even if you have met the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). This is the same for employees.The MediSave amount above the BHS will be transferred to your CPF Special Account (SA)* or Retirement Account (RA). The BHS cap and overflow arrangement are intentionally planned to avoid over savings in MediSave and to supplement your retirement savings. These overflows which end up in your SA or RA can be withdrawn according to thewithdrawal guidelines. If you’ve met the Full Retirement Sum in your SA or RA, the savings in excess of the BHS will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA). Savings in the OA can be used for other purposes such as housing repayment.*The SA will be closed for members aged 55 and above from early 2025. Read morehere.

questions.question: Can I withdraw my CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments when I reach 55 years old?
questions.answer: You can apply to the Board to withdraw your CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) and CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA) investments as well as the cash balance in your Investment Account, as long as you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in the Retirement Account (RA). The FRS can be set aside fully with cash, or with cash (i.e. at least the Basic Retirement Sum) and property. Your CPF Investment Account will be closed once you apply to withdraw your investments.Please refer to thisFAQfor more information on how the retirement sum is set aside at age 55.You will be able to view the link to submit your application through theInvestment dashboardif you meet the eligibility conditions.Please refer to the following information to find out what would happen after you have applied for withdrawal of investments under the CPFIS:CPFIS-OAWe will inform the agent bank to close your CPF Investment Account. The agent bank will contact you for the withdrawal of your investments and cash balance (if any) in your CPF Investment Account. Your investments will be transferred* to your own name and you may thereafter liquidate them as you wish and have the sale proceeds paid to you directly.Once withdrawn, your CPFIS investments and cash balance in your CPF Investment Account will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.* Central Depository (Pte) Ltd (“CDP”) imposes a transfer fee of $10.00 (excluding GST) for every share counter transferred from your CPF Investment Account to your CDP Account.CPFIS-SAWe will inform your product provider(s) to transfer your investments to your own name and you may thereafter liquidate them as you wish and have the sale proceeds paid to you directly.Once withdrawn, your CPFIS investments will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.

questions.question: I am earning close to the qualifying wage cap, why is my Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) so low?
questions.answer: To best support lower-wage workers, the WIS benefits are gradually reduced as the wage levels of the workers increase nearer to the qualifying wage cap. The gradual reduction ensures that the lower-wage workers do not see a sharp reduction in their WIS benefits when they upgrade their skills and begin to earn more. Taken together, the total amount of the income and the WIS benefits would still increase overall as one's income increases.

questions.question: Are CPF contributions payable if I am working in Singapore for an overseas platform operator?
questions.answer: CPF contributions are required on net earnings to any Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident doing platform work in Singapore, even if the platform operator is located overseas. You should communicate your CPF rights clearly to the overseas platform operator before the start of your platform work to avoid subsequent disputes.You should also research your prospective platform operator to ensure that it has legitimate business presence in Singapore and is registered with Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). If your CPF contributions are not paid on time or discrepancies are found, please approach your platform operator for clarification immediately while documentary evidence is fresh. If your platform operator does not provide you with a satisfactory explanation, you can lodge a report with CPF Board or MOM.Do note that CPF Board may not be able to assist you in claims against an overseas platform operator with no presence in Singapore and who is not registered with ACRA. You may wish to exercise caution when working with such platform operators.

questions.question: For CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit, how do I derive the employee's share to be refunded to me?
questions.answer: For example, if you are a Singaporean Citizen who is below 55 years old and has received a total of $40,000 of CPF contributions for 2023, the excess contributions to be refunded to you can be estimated based on the calculation below:Step 1: Total excess CPF contributions refunded to the employer= Total CPF contributions paid – CPF Annual Limit= $40,000 – $37,740= $2,260Step 2: Employee’s share to be refunded= (Total excess CPF contributions refunded ÷ applicable CPF contribution rate) x applicable employee CPF contribution rate= ($2,260 ÷ 37%) x 20%= $1,221* (cents should be dropped)You can also verify the above estimated employee’s share of refund by computing the difference between the total employee’s share of contributions paid and employee’s share of contributions payable. The employee’s share of contributions payable can be computed using theAdditional Wage ceiling Calculator.1This rate is applicable for an employee who is a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (3rd year onwards) and is 55 or below.

questions.question: After the transfer of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme investments to CPF Investment Scheme, what will happen to the sale proceeds if I subsequently sell those investments?
questions.answer: All the sale proceeds will be refunded to your CPF Accounts. You can subsequently withdraw the monies subject to CPF withdrawal rules.

questions.question: Can I nominate beneficiaries to the proceeds of my Part V insurance policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.answer: You may nominate beneficiaries as long as:No legal or equitable trust, including but not limited to statutory trusts under any written law, is created over the Part V insurance policy; andYour insurer allows you to do so.

questions.question: Can I enjoy tax relief as a self-employed person when I contribute to my MediSave Account to offset my outstanding MediSave payable, pre-pay my future MediSave payable or make voluntary top-ups to my CPF accounts?
questions.answer: Self-employed persons (SEPs) can enjoy tax relief on their MediSave or CPF contributions based on their annual net trade income (NTI). However, there is no tax relief for your MediSave or CPF contributions if your assessed NTI for the year of assessment is zero or negative.You can enjoy tax relief on your MediSave or CPF contributions based on whichever is lower:37% of assessable income; orCPF Annual Limit of $37,740; orActual amount contributed by youPlease note that there will be a personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 which will apply from Year of Assessment 2018. This cap applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed, including any relief on voluntary contributions made on or after 1 January 2017.As accepted MediSave or CPF contributions cannot be refunded, you should evaluate whether you would benefit from tax relief on your voluntary CPF top-ups and make an informed decision. Please visit theInland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS)website for more information.

questions.question: I have outstanding MediSave payable. Why am I not allowed to make partial payment to offset my MediSave payable under the Manage your MediSave Payable form (MMSP)?
questions.answer: This is to encourage and make it easier for self-employed persons to be up-to-date with their MediSave payable. You can conveniently request instalment plan or make full payment for your MediSave payable viaManage your MediSave Payable(MMSP). This allows for hassle-free licence application/renewal while being up-to-date with your MediSave payable.

questions.question: How do I opt in to increase my CPF contributions as a platform worker and how soon will it take effect?
questions.answer: You can opt in using theplatform worker opt-in form.If you opt inon or beforethe 15thof a month, the increased contributions will start from the next month.If you opt inafterthe 15thof a month, the increased contributions will start two months later.For example, if you opt in on 15 April, the increased contributions will start from 1 May. If you opt in on 16 April, the increased contributions will start from 1 June.You can use theOpt-in Status Checkerto confirm whether you have opted in and view your opt-in effective month.Note: For opted-in platform workers joining anewplatform operator, the increased CPF contributions will apply depending on when you onboard the new platform operator. If you onboard on or before the 15thof the month, the increased CPF contributions will be made in the following month. If you onboard after the 15thof the month, the increased contributions will be made two months after. For example:If you onboard on 14thFebruary, your increased contributions will apply from 1stMarch. Non-opt-in contribution rates will apply for the month of February.If you onboard on 16thFebruary, your increased contributions will apply from 1stApril. Non-opt-in contribution rates will apply for the month of February and March.

questions.question: How may I repay the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) of my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy?
questions.answer: You may repay the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) by paying cash to the insurance company directly. The cash balance in your CPF Investment Scheme Investment Account cannot be used to repay the APL.

questions.question: What actions do I (as a CPFIS investor) need to take due to reduction in Total Expense Ratio caps?
questions.answer: You do not have to take any action unless the fund(s) you have invested in cannot comply with the reduced Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps.In which case, the relevant parties (i.e. Fund Management Companies/insurers/investment administrators) will notify you by letters. As existing funds which are unable to comply with the new TER caps from 2016 will be downgraded to List B and will not be allowed to take innewCPF monies from then, you will be given the following options by the relevant parties:Free switches to other funds included under CPF Investment Scheme within a specified period from the date of the letter (around one month)Redeem the unitsContinue to remain invested in these funds (if you choose this option, no further action is required from you)Note: Cash investors would not be affected.For info - List of funds will be updated when necessary.List A and B unit trusts(PDF, 0.2MB)List A and B Investment Link Products (ILPs) Sub-funds(PDF, 0.1MB)

questions.question: Do I still have to contribute to my MediSave if I am both a self-employed person as well as an employee working in another company?
questions.answer: If you earn an annualnet trade incomeof more than $6,000, you are required to contribute to your MediSave Account as a self-employed person (SEP).CPF contribution is based on your total income. Therefore, an SEP who is also an employee at the same time, is required to contribute to MediSave as an SEP. This is the same for employees who hold more than one job and are required to pay CPF contributions for all the wages they receive.However, you can apply to limit the MediSave payable on your self-employed income if your total employment income (excluding Additional Wages*) for the year exceeds the maximum total annual income. You may refer to thisFAQfor more information on the conditions for this application.*Additional Wages are wage supplements which are not granted wholly and exclusively for the month. Examples are the annual bonus, leave pay, incentive and other payments made at intervals of more than a month.To limit your MediSave contributions, you maywrite to us.

questions.question: How do I start investing my CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings in Treasury bills (T-bills) under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.answer: You need to be at least 18 years old; not an undischarged bankrupt; and have more than $20,000 in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA). If you meet all of the conditions and would like to start investing your CPF OA savings in T-bills, please take the following steps:Step 1:Complete CPFISSelf-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)to assess if CPFIS is suitable for you. You cancheck your SAQ completion status.Step 2:Open CPF Investment Account (CPFIA) online with any of the three CPFIS agent banks:DBS's digibot(scroll to “Get started with CPFIA” and click “digibot”)OCBC's websiteor OCBC's mobile appUOB's websiteAlternatively, you may also visit any of the banks (DBS, OCBC or UOB) branches to open your CPF Investment Account.Step 3:Invest in the T-bills of your choice. The Government issues 6-months and 1-year T-bills. You can check theMAS websiteon upcoming T-bills auctions. After deciding, you can use the bank’s online services to apply for T-bills. Refer toHow to use your CPF for T-bills.Step 4:Wait for the results of your T-bills purchase, which will be available on auction date. The bank will notify you on the outcome of your T-bills purchase. You can also check the T-bills allotted to you via your CPF Investment Account (CPFIA) online. Your CPF OA would be deducted and transferred to your CPFIA only upon successful allotment of the T-bills. The deducted amount (i.e., initial investment amount) would be lower than the amount which you have been allotted as T-bills are issued at a discount to the face value. Refer to theT-bills FAQs on the MAS websiteon how to compute your initial investment amount based on cut-off yield (T-bills FAQs > Application of T-bills > “How do I compute my initial investment for my T-bills based on the cut-off yield?”).Step 5:Upon maturity of your T-bills in 6 or 12 months (depending on the type of T-bills that you have purchased), your CPFIS agent bank will credit the proceeds to your IA. You can then take any of the following actions:Re-invest in another T-bill purchase or any other investment.If you do not plan to re-invest your CPF OA savings, you can apply to return the balances in the CPFIA to CPF OA to earn the CPF interest. You can do so via your CPFIS agent bank’s ATMs, internet/phone banking or over the bank counter. ClickDBSandOCBC’s links to find out more.If you do nothing, the monies in your CPFIA will be automatically returned to your CPF OA, if your CPFIA is inactive for 2 consecutive months.

questions.question: Why must I earn more than $500 from at least one platform to receive Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is intended to offset part of the year-on-year increase in a platform worker’s own share of CPF contributions to his Ordinary and Special accounts. How much a platform worker will contribute to his CPF will be based on his net earnings from each platform.A platform worker whose net earnings from each platform is less than or equal to $500 does not have to make his own share of CPF contributions. Given there is no increase in the platform worker’s share of his CPF contributions, he will not be eligible for PCTS.

questions.question: I am aged 55 and above. What happens to my CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account after my Special Account is closed?
questions.answer: If you are aged 55 and above, you can continue to hold your existing CPF Investment Scheme-Special Account (CPFIS-SA) investments until you decide to sell them or until they mature. Upon sale or maturity, your proceeds would be paid to your Retirement Account (RA) up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), with any remaining balance paid to your Ordinary Account (OA).Before theclosure of SA, CPF savings in SA can be used to invest after setting aside the FRS in your Retirement Account. With the closure of SA, your SA savings would be transferred to the OA once you have set aside the FRS in your RA and you can use them to invest under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA).

questions.question: Why is there an annual cap of $2,000 of matching grant. Would the Government consider allowing eligible members to top up $20,000 at once and receive the lifetime matching grant of $20,000?
questions.answer: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is targeted at seniors with lower retirement savings to help them save more for retirement. As member’s circumstances such as income and housing can change over time, the annual cap ensures that the scheme will help seniors who require the support over a longer period.

questions.question: How will the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme affect my income declaration to IRAS for tax purposes?
questions.answer: There will be no change to Self-Employed Person (SEP)’s declaration of income for tax purposes. SEPs should continue to declare his annual income earned up to 31stDecember of the preceding year in the Income Tax Return for the current Year of Assessment (YA). For example, the SEP needs to declare his gross income for services provided between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 in Income Tax Return for YA2025, even if it is invoiced only in January 2025. This is regardless of when the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions for the said services are made.

questions.question: With the closure of my Special Account, can I have the option to top up more than the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.answer: You are not able to top up more than the current year’sEnhanced Retirement Scheme (ERS)as the CPF system is designed to cater to the basic retirement needs of the broad majority of Singaporeans.With the raising of the ERS on 1 January 2025 from three times to four times of the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) (that is $426,000 in 2025), more than 99% of CPF members aged 55 or above will be able to transfer all their Special Account savings to their Retirement Account to continue to earn the higher long-term interest rate and receive higher payouts, should they wish to do so.You may consider transferring the savings in excess of the raised ERS to your loved ones’ CPF accounts, keep them in your OA to continue to earn 2.5% interest each year while retaining the flexibility to withdraw anytime. Alternatively, you can invest them under the CPF Investment Scheme – Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA), if you have assessed that CPFIS is suitable for you.

questions.question: What is the GIRO bank account used for my recurring cash top-up arrangement?
questions.answer: If you have an existing GIRO arrangement, you can view your current bank account used for your GIRO by accessingSet up GIRO for cash top-ups for retirement form, under “Select bank”.

questions.question: How can I check the amount that I can top up to my Retirement Account to reach the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2025?
questions.answer: You may check your top-up limit on yourRetirement Dashboardon 1 January 2025 once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.Find outhow the top-up limit is computed.

questions.question: What happens if the MediSave contributions I made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) are lower than my MediSave payable for the year?
questions.answer: If your total CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable for the latest year, you will be required to top up the remaining amount. You’ll be notified accordingly, and you can choose to make payment via a lump-sum payment(s) or sign up for monthly GIRO instalments.Example:Based on his estimated income of $21,000 for 2023, Sam contributed $2,100 via CAYE. In the following year, he declared that he earned a higher NTI of $30,000 for 2023. As such, Sam’s MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $3,000. Sam will have to top up the shortfall of $900.This example is illustrated within the table below:Estimated 2023 NTI$21,000CAYE contributions in 2023$2,100(After 2023 NTI declaration)Declared 2023 NTI$30,000MediSave payable for work done in 2023$3,000Shortfall Sam has to top up$900(i.e. $3,000 - $2,100)

questions.question: I am a part-time platform worker. Will I be eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: As eligibility is not based on working hours, even if you are a part-time or ad-hoc platform worker, you can qualify for the Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) as long as you meet the following criteria at the point of assessment:Are a Singapore Citizen;Born in 1995 or later; or born before 1995 andoptedinto increase your CPF contributions;Net income from platform work and other employment sources does not exceed $3,000 for the month (Net income refers to gross earnings minus the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount); andHave an increase in your share of CPF contributions to the Ordinary and Special Accounts as compared to the previous year.As PCTS is intended to offset the increase in CPF contributions, a platform worker will not receive PCTS for the months where his net earnings for a platform operator are$500 or less, as he does not have to make his own share of CPF contributions.In addition, platform workers aged above 65 will not be eligible as they will not see an increase in their own share of CPF contributions if they opt in to increased CPF contributions. In 2025, platform workers aged above 60 to 65 will also not see an increase in their own share of CPF contributions, and thus they will not be eligible.

questions.question: What happens if I make a voluntary housing refund when I am 55 years old and above?
questions.answer: The refund amount will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to meet your cohort’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This transfer will help boost your retirement savings and provide you with a higher monthly payout upon reaching your payout eligibility age.When you turn 55 years old, you can withdraw at least $5,000 or any amount in excess after setting aside your FRS. Check the amount you can withdraw by logging in to yourRetirement dashboard.

questions.question: How can I check my existing recurring cash top-up arrangements for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.answer: You can check your existing recurring cash top-up arrangements, including the recipients, amount of cash top-ups, and frequency (monthly or yearly) by accessing theManage recurring cash top-ups for retirementform, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.

questions.question: Why is tax relief removed for cash top-ups that attract matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme from 2025?
questions.answer: As the cash top-ups serve to boost the retirement adequacy of seniors through the matching grant, tax relief is removed for cash top-ups which attract the matching grant. This is because the matching grant is already a benefit extended by the Government. Givers may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for cash top-ups that do not attract the MRSS matching grant, if they meet the criteria under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme (e.g., if the recipient has not met the current Full Retirement Sum).Learn more onhow the matching grant and tax relief are determined.Find out more on theconditions to qualify for tax relief.

questions.question: Where can I see my special dividend as declared by Singtel on 10 November 2022?
questions.answer: Singtel declared a special dividend of $0.05 per share for financial year ending 31 March 2023. According to Singtel, the special dividend will be paid in tranches. The first S$0.025 will be paid along with the interim dividend in December 2022, while the remaining S$0.025 will be paid out together with Singtel’s final dividend in August 2023. The special dividend in both tranches is payable based on their respective book closure dates. For more information on Singtel’s special dividend, you can refer toSingtel website.If you have discounted Singtel shares in your CPF account during these periods, you will receive Singtel’s special dividend along with your interim/final dividend in your Ordinary Account. Please check your CPF statement.

questions.question: Do I have to refund the housing grant to my CPF account when I make a voluntary housing refund of the monies withdrawn for my property?
questions.answer: When you make a voluntary housing refund, you can refund up to the principal CPF withdrawn towards the property (including the CPF Housing Grant) plus its accrued interest to your CPF account.Generally, the housing grant will be refunded to your Ordinary Account. If you have received more than $30,000 in housing grants, part of the housing grants may be credited to your Special Account/Retirement Account and MediSave Account. Check yourHome ownership dashboardto see the amount that will be credited to your Special/Retirement Account and MediSave Account.These savings that are credited to yourSpecial Account/Retirement Account and MediSave Accountcan then be used for approved purposes under the various CPF approved schemes to help you with your healthcare and retirement needs.

questions.question: If I have an existing regular premium insurance policy bought using cash, can I continue to service the future premiums using CPF under the CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)?
questions.answer: With effect from 1 January 2001, CPF savings cannot be used for new regular premium insurance policies, regardless of whether the policies are converted from cash or newly bought from insurance companies.

questions.question: Will my discounted Singtel shares be sold or liquidated when I apply to withdraw my discounted Singtel shares upon meeting CPF withdrawal conditions?
questions.answer: Withdrawing your discounted Singtel shares will not result in liquidation of your shares. It is a request to the Board to transfer the discounted Singtel shares to your CDP securities account. Once the shares have been transferred, you will receive a statement from CDP and the Board.

questions.question: When will CPF Board start issuing the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons digitally?
questions.answer: Since 1 November 2024, CPF Board has been issuing the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons digitally.You will receive an email or SMS notification to view your digital notice via theself-employment dashboardwhen it is ready.If you wish to receive a hardcopy notice instead, please update your notification preference by completing thenotification preference form. Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons.

questions.question: How can i make a voluntary housing refund of the housing amount withdrawn if i am not selling my property?
questions.answer: You can refund any amount, capped at the full principal amount you have withdrawn for the property with the accrued interest. You can submit your application:1.Onlineby following the steps below:Read the disclaimer. If you accept, click the checkboxClick "Start"Log in with your SingpassSelect a payment methodSelect a property, enter a refund amountClick "Next"Read the declaration. If you agree, click the checkbox and click "Confirm"Make the payment2. Through CPF Mobile app by following the steps below:Log in to CPF Mobile app with your SingpassSelect "Services"Select "Voluntary Housing Refund" and click "Continue"Select the property, key in a refund amount, and click "Next"Read the agreement. If you agree, click the checkboxClick "Next"Select the payment methodMake the paymentIf you make the refunds by PayNow using the QR code or OCBC Digital, the transaction will be shown in your transaction history immediately after the payment.Members who are unable to submit online or through the CPF Mobile app may write to us atcpf.gov.sg/writetousfor assistance.

questions.question: Why are there no deductions from my bank account even though I have successfully made a recurring cash top-up arrangement?
questions.answer: It could be due to one of the following reasons:If you have just made recurring cash top-up arrangements, the GIRO deduction might not have started yet. You may check the start month of your recurring cash top-up by accessing theManage recurring cash top-ups for retirementform, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.If you have updated your GIRO bank account after 8th of the month, deductions will start from the following month instead of the current month.Find out more.

questions.question: Will self-employed persons who provide services to the private sector be mandated to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.answer: The Government, as a service buyer, has piloted Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) since 1 January 2020. There are currently no plans to extend CAYE into the private sector. Nonetheless, companies in the private sector are encouraged to voluntarily adopt CAYE.

questions.question: How much tax relief can I enjoy when I make cash top-ups?
questions.answer: You can enjoy an equivalent amount of tax relief for cash top-ups made in each calendar year of up to:$8,000 if you make a top-up to yourself; andan additional $8,000 if you make a cash top-up to yourloved ones.Please note that only cash top-ups up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS) are eligible for tax relief.Log in with your Singpassto find out how much you can top up to yourself. If you make cash top-ups to your loved ones, please note that the tax relief does not apply to your recipients. Find out theconditions to qualify for tax relief.If your employer or platform operator made a cash top-up on your behalf, you could receive up to $8,000* of tax relief per calendar year. If you are an employer or platform operator making cash top-ups to your employees' or platform workers’ Special/ Retirement accounts, youmay claim tax deduction on the cash top-ups when filing your company’s income tax return.* Includes any tax relief that the employee or platform worker would enjoy for cash top-ups made to himself.From 1 January 2025, givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $2,000 per year) under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will no longer receive tax relief. Find out more onhow this works.

questions.question: Why do I still have outstanding MediSave payable when I am already on Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.answer: Your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions is an estimate of your MediSave payable for the year and may be lower or higher than your MediSave payable for the year. If your CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable for the year, you’ll be required to top up the shortfall. You’ll also be required to make MediSave contributions for any outstanding MediSave payable incurred in previous years.

questions.question: Is it compulsory to keep switching funds under the CPF Investment Scheme if the funds which I am holding do not meet the stricter criteria?
questions.answer: You can opt to hold on to your existing funds without switching.

questions.question: Which of my CPF accounts can I use to participate under CPF Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) or CPF Investment Scheme - Special Account (CPFIS-SA)?
questions.answer: You can only use your Ordinary Account (OA) savings for investments under CPF Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA), and your Special Account (SA) savings for investments under CPF Investment Scheme - Special Account (CPFIS-SA).The instruments available for investments under CPFIS-OA and CPFIS-SA are different. You may not combine savings from your OA and SA to buy a product. However, you can transfer funds from your OA to your SA* to invest under CPFIS-SA. Such transfers are irreversible. The total savings in the SA including the amount withdrawn under CPFIS-SA cannot exceed the current full retirement sum after the transfer.* Applicable only to members below age 55.

questions.question: Why do employees receive monthly Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) payments while Self-Employed Persons receive their WIS once a year?
questions.answer: The incomes of employees are automatically computed based on their monthly CPF contributions from their employers. This enables CPF Board to assess their Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) eligibility automatically and disburse their WIS on a monthly basis.On the other hand, the net trade income (NTI) of a Self-Employed Person (SEP) is assessed over an entire year and can only be determined the following year after the current year has ended.

questions.question: I am a homemaker/babysitter. Can I qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme?
questions.answer: Allowances received for carrying out family support roles such as babysitting and general caregiving for dependants are considered transfers within the family. They are not external sources of income derived from employment, hence it would not be appropriate to consider these transfers for Workfare Income Supplement scheme.The Government recognises that such family roles are important. There are other forms of government support for these roles, such as theMarriage and Parenthood packagewhich provides broad-based support for couples to raise and care for their children.Employee/Self-Employed Persons who are also caregivers (generally include caregivers residing with care recipients who are medically certified to have permanent moderate to severe disabilities) could qualify for concessionary WIS, even if they earn less than $500. For more information, please refer to our FAQshere.

questions.question: What are the reasons for the Board selecting these new criteria for new funds which wants to be included under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.answer: The new criteria cover issues that the Board is most concerned with, such as quality, consistency of performance relative to peer group and investment costs.

questions.question: I have made a voluntary top-up to my CPF accounts, why does the voluntary contribution allocated to my MediSave account not offset my MediSave payable?
questions.answer: With effect from 29 May 2024, the member and self-employed person’s “Contribute to my three CPF accounts” forms have been combined and renamed as “Top up CPF accounts”. This is to simplify the process in making voluntary top-ups, regardless of whether you are earning income as a self-employed person. You will continue to enjoy self-employed tax relief on these voluntary top-ups if you meet theeligibility criteria.As these top-ups are voluntary in nature, the voluntary contribution allocated to your MediSave Account will not be used to offset your mandatory MediSave payable, and consequently will not meet the MediSave requirement for Workfare for self-employed persons. The intent is for self-employed persons to prioritise their mandatory MediSave contributions over voluntary contributions, and help self-employed persons to first set aside sufficient savings for their healthcare needs. Self-employed persons who wish to make mandatory contributions towards their MediSave payable, and to qualify for Workfare, should do so via theManage your MediSave payable, instead of making voluntary contributions.

questions.question: Can I use my CPF monies to service the premiums of my Part V Insurance Policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.answer: You can use your CPF monies in your Ordinary Account to service the future premiums of your policies (including endowment, whole life or rider policies, and regular premium policies).

questions.question: To qualify for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), what is considered income?
questions.answer: We will automatically assess your eligibility for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) based on the net earnings declared by your platform operator(s) when making CPF contributions, and the wages declared by your employer when making CPF contributions if you also work as an employee.Your platform operator will compute your monthly platform net earnings based on your monthly gross earnings less aFixed Expense DeductionAmount(FEDA). The FEDA depends on the mode of transportation you use for platform work.Your wages from your employer are the total amount of wages for any calendar month, which is the sum of your Ordinary Wages for the month and the Additional Wage paid to you in that month.

questions.question: Can I change the life insured under my Part V insurance policy under Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS)?
questions.answer: The life insured must be the CPF member whose CPF savings are used to pay premiums.

questions.question: What should I do if I wish to receive the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons in hardcopy?
questions.answer: If you wish to receive your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons via hardcopy instead, you may update your notification preference via thenotification preference formusing your Singpass. The hardcopy notice will be mailed to you at your residential address.Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions thereafter.

questions.question: My Singapore Permanent Resident status was reinstated with a new Re-Entry Permit. Which issue date should I refer to determine my CPF contribution rates?
questions.answer: CPF contributions will be payable from the day your Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status was reinstated.However, to determine the year of SPR status, you should refer to the date indicated on your valid Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority of Singapore (ICA).

questions.question: My platform operator did not pay my CPF contributions. What can I do to qualify for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: We will assess your eligibility for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) based on the earnings declared by your platform operator when making CPF contributions. If you are not paid your CPF contributions on time, you should approach your platform operator for an explanation and ask when your platform operator will be making the payment.If your platform operator does not provide you with a satisfactory response, you can lodge a report with CPF Board. The Board takes a serious view of platform operators who default on CPF contributions. The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement actionwould be taken against platform operators who fail to pay by the 14thof the following month (or the next working day if the 14thfalls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date. In cases where the company is in financial difficulty, CPF arrears may not always be recoverable despite our enforcement efforts.You mayfind out moreon your rights and platform operators’ obligations under the CPF Act and the Platform Workers Act.

questions.question: How does regular MediSave co-contributions received under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme benefit me?
questions.answer: Under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme, the regular MediSave co-contributions from your taxi operator can:Offset your mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed SchemeEarn up to 6%1interest per annum (p.a.) on your MediSave savings.This includes an additional 1% interest p.a. on the first $60,000 of your combined balances (with up to $20,000 from the Ordinary Account).CPF members aged 55 and above will also earn an additional 1% interest p.a. on the first $30,000 of their combined CPF balances.Pay MediShield Life/Integrated Shield Plan premiums for you and your loved ones (spouse, children, parents, grandparents, or siblings)Qualify2to receive Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) payouts in cash and in your MediSave Account1Based on the current 4% interest rate floor for MediSave savings. Refer tocpf.gov.sg/interestratesfor the current rates.2Terms and conditions apply. Refer tocpf.gov.sg/wisfor more information.

questions.question: Can I withdraw my sale proceeds or investment profits from my discounted Singtel shares?
questions.answer: The sale proceeds and investment profits form part of your CPF savings. You can apply to withdraw them from age 55 if you meet thewithdrawal conditions.For more information on how you can withdraw your CPF retirement savings, please refer to thisFAQ.

questions.question: How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.answer: You can make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ Retirement Account (RA) via theCPF website or CPF mobile app. Your cash top-up will generally be credited almost instantly upon successful payment.Considermaking regular monthly or yearly cash top-ups conveniently via GIRO, without the hassle of completing the application form every time you top up.You may want to check whether you or your loved ones areeligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Schemebefore making a cash top-up.To make a top-up, you can refer to the following table:Application modePayment viaGuideWebRecurring cash top-upsvia GIROGuideOne-time cash top-upvia PayNow QRGuide(PDF, 0.1MB)Video GuideCPF Mobile appPayNow QROCBC DigitalEnglishChineseMalayTamilCPF transferGuide

questions.question: Why are Singapore Permanent Residents not eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: The Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) scheme is only for Singaporean lower-income platform workers.If you require financial assistance, please contact the ComCare hotline at 1800-222-0000, or emailAsk_SSO@msf.gov.sg.

questions.question: What are the service standards for processing applications relating to CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.answer: Please refer to the table for our service standards for processing applications relating to CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS).ServiceNormal Processing TimeWithdraw CPF investmentsWithin 3 working daysUpdate Stock / Gold LimitsWithin 2 working daysTransfer CPFIS Sale Proceeds(Division of CPF-related Matrimonial Assets)Within 15 working days

questions.question: Will my cash top-ups or CPF transfers be refunded to me if the recipient passes away?
questions.answer: Cash top-ups and CPF transfers will generally be treated as gifts to the recipient. Any unused cash top-ups and CPF transfers will be paid to the recipient's nominees based on hisCPF nomination. This is subject tosafeguards to prevent premature withdrawals.

questions.question: Why is CPF Board reducing the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps?
questions.answer: Reducing the Total Expense Ratio caps is part of CPF Board's continuous efforts to lower the cost of investing under the CPF Investment Scheme. This would help enhance returns, hence enable CPF members who have invested in the fund to accumulate their retirement savings faster.

questions.question: If I am eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme this year, will I be automatically eligible in the following years?
questions.answer: No, your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is assessed annually. We will notify you at the beginning of the year if you are eligible.

questions.question: Will the new admission criteria be applied to existing funds under CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.answer: The new criteria will apply to existing funds from 1 January 2011. To help members make better informed investment decisions, the Board will, in due course, step up its member education efforts and also avail relevant information on the performance and expense ratios of existing funds.

questions.question: What is the Annual Value (AV) of a property and why is the AV of my place of residence used to assess my eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: Annual Value (AV) is the estimated gross annual rent of the property if it were to be rented out, excluding furniture, furnishings and maintenance fees. It is determined based on estimated market rentals of similar or comparable properties. It can be found on the property tax bill you receive each year.AV serves as a housing criterion that targets lower-wage workers with less household wealth.For more information on the computation of AV, please visit theInland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website.

questions.question: Why do I still need to contribute to MediSave as a self-employed person even though I have already bought insurance for myself?
questions.answer: All working Singapore residents are required to contribute to their MediSave as a form of savings for their own and their loved ones’ healthcare needs.Many Singaporeans have bought private hospital insurance plans in the form of Integrated Shield Plans, or IPs. IPs comprise of two parts – MediShield Life (MSL) which is a universal basic health insurance plan, and additional private insurance coverage. MediSave can be used to pay the premiums for both MSL and private insurance, up to the current withdrawal limit.Hence, private medical insurance serves to complement rather than replace your MediSave savings.

questions.question: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if my retirement savings are above the current Basic Retirement Sum?
questions.answer: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is designed to help senior Singapore Citizens with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts. If your retirement savings are more than the current Basic Retirement Sum, you will not be eligible for the scheme as it is intended to provide additional support to those who need it the most.

questions.question: What is the approach taken by CPF Board in enforcing MediSave contributions from self-employed persons?
questions.answer: Each year, self-employed persons (SEPs) are notified by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) via the Notice of Computation (NOC) to pay their MediSave payable in full or by monthly instalments through GIRO. The CPF Board may enforce payments from SEPs only if they have failed to make payments after repeated reminders.

questions.question: How do I know if the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution amount and net service fee payment amount are made correctly?
questions.answer: You can check your payment records by logging in to theSelf-employment dashboardusing your Singpass, underContribute As You Earn > Show all payments.If you’ve previously informed CPF Board of your contact details, you’ll also receive a notification whenever a contribution to your MediSave Account has been made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). If you wish to update your contact details, you can do so via logging on tomy cpfdigital servicesusing your Singpass.

questions.question: Why is my spouse's income and property ownership used to determine my eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.answer: To ensure that Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is targeted at recipients with limited access to household wealth, you will not qualify for WIS if:the assessable income of your spouse for the preceding Year of Assessment exceeds $70,000; oryou and your spouse together own two or more properties.

questions.question: As a self-employed person who provides services to Government agencies, how will I be enrolled into Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.answer: You’ll be automatically enrolled into Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) when you receive a service payment from a Government agency you have provided services to as a self-employed person (SEP). You’ll receive a notification from CPF Board when you receive your first payment via CAYE. Subsequently, you’ll also receive a notification each time you receive a payment via CAYE.

questions.question: How and when will I be notified on my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.answer: If you have registered your contact details with CPF Board, you will receive a notificationvia SMSoremailwhen your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment has been credited.

questions.question: Will I be eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if I am turning 55 later this year?
questions.answer: Yes, you will be eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme as long as you are 55 years old in the assessment year and meet theeligibility criteria.If you are turning 55 this year and your Retirement Account has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.You can check your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) via theMRSS eligiblity checker(no Singpass required) andRetirement Dashboard.

questions.question: I worked as both an employee as well as a self-employed person (SEP) in the work year. When will I receive my Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) for the work year?
questions.answer: You will receive monthly Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) payments based on your employee income if you meet the WIS eligibility criteria for the work year (WY).If you are also an eligible dual status worker (DSW) who has worked concurrently as an SEP and employee in the year, you may receive additional WIS if your combined employment and net trade income results in a higher WIS payment. You will receive the additional WIS payment after you have declared your income and made the required MediSave contributions.You will receive WIS once a year for work done as an SEP in the preceding year. The earliest payment for SEPs/DSWs for a particular WY will be on 30 April WY+1*.*Payment via PayNow NRIC-linked bank account or bank crediting will be credited by end of the month while payment via GovCash will be on the 3rd of the following month.

questions.question: How do I apply for refund on my share of CPF contributions that was paid above the CPF wage ceiling(s)?
questions.answer: You will need to applyonlinefor refund of CPF contributions paid above the CPF Wage Ceiling(s).

questions.question: Do I need to apply for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.answer: You do not need to apply for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS).We will automatically assess your eligibility for PCTS based on the net earnings declared by your platform operator when making CPF contributions.We will credit your PCTS payment to yourPayNow NRIC-linked bank accountif you have one. Otherwise, it will be credited to the bank account that you have registered to receive Government benefits, or viaGovCashif you had not registered a bank account with us. Crediting of PCTS will not go through your platform operators.

questions.question: I made a cash top-up to my spouse/sibling between 1 January 2024 and 16 February 2024 and instructed that I did not wish to claim tax relief. With the increase in income threshold from $4,000 to $8,000, how can I amend my instruction to claim tax relief?
questions.answer: You cansubmit an applicationto amend your instructions to claim tax relief for top-ups made in 2024, if your recipient’s income in 2023 is between $4,000 and $8,000 (inclusive).If you indicated that you have a GIRO arrangement to make regular top-ups to your spouse or sibling in the application, your instructions for the GIRO arrangement will also be amended to claim tax relief for future GIRO top-ups.Please note thatother conditions to qualify for tax relief apply.

questions.question: Why is there no tax relief for top-ups to the MediSave Account made to my children or non-immediate family?
questions.answer: Tax relief is an incentive given to encourage members to build up their healthcare savings for themselves or their immediate family members, particularly older Singaporeans who may have less healthcare savings.However, your children have longer remaining working lifespans and would have more time to build up their healthcare savings for their own healthcare needs. Hence, there is no tax relief for top-ups made to your children or non-immediate family members.

questions.question: If I am concurrently a full-time employee doing platform work, do I still need to make CPF contributions on platform earnings?
questions.answer: Yes, your platform operator will deduct the required CPF contributions from your net earnings from platform work. There is no change to your CPF contributions as an employee. Your employer must still deduct and make CPF contributions for you.

questions.question: Can I pledge my Academic Staff Provident Fund Approved Investment Scheme (ASPFAIS) Part V insurance policy?
questions.answer: Pledging of Part V insurance policies is not allowed under the CPF Investment Scheme.
